I’ve loved Hadestown since I first listened to the cast recording. I loved Hadestown enough to book a cross-country flight, and a Broadway ticket, the only time in my life I traveled to see theatre (largely as I knew I’d never see Patrick Page as Frollo and didn’t want to miss him as Hades too). I’m so grateful that I had the means to do so, and prioritized the multi-day trek to see the singular live production.

And, while I’m glad we’re getting some recordings of top musicals (I’ve already got my Six ticket!), the inaccessibility of Broadway has always killed me. I believe in my bones that this privatization of art is wrong. I’ve never bought the argument that it would lead to fewer people seeing shows live. A better democratization of shows would lead to another generation of kids who will, in turn, be inspired to make the next decade(s) of art.

This is 2026 where the costs of recording live theatre are near 0. With a simple three-camera setup, and a bit of editing, you could forever preserve so much currently lost art. I truly hope someone had the foresight to record Josh Grobin’s Sweeney Todd because I would pay so much money to watch that (and another few dozen) original/revival casts.

There’s how I understand the movie now, with two decades passed and far more Americans considering the Iraq War to be a mistake (being anti-Iraq got both Obama and Trump elected), and how I would’ve processed the movie had I watched it at the time. I think this may’ve been a 9/10 for me in 2008, but there’s now a few angles that it’s obvious that the filmmakers missed (e.g. the 100k-1M Iraqi civilians that died, what we were even doing in Iraq in the first place) largely from making this movie so soon after the real world events had occurred. reviews.filmTitle: Katrina: Come Hell and High Water
paragraphs: This doc really puts a personal spin on the Katrina tragedy and tells the events at a slow, impactful clip. You also get to check in on the city twenty years later and learn how the storm permanently impacted New Orleans. But for the one vaccine story, the anecdotes were all really compelling.

The execution of One Battle After Another was simply phenomenal. Such a well paced interesting story and (scarily prophetic) world, with very even screen time for all of the leads. It did a great job of sequencing the events in a way that kept the stress high and building at all times. Penn was an incredible villain, and DiCaprio played a hilariously bumbling lead with all the heart required.
Definitely want a repeat viewing of this one (though there’s no way I’ll be able to squeeze it in during the theatrical release).

These Disney (and now DreamWorks) live action remakes are the most uninspired cash-grabs, where changes feel extremely unnecessary. And then every time they carbon copy the original, I’m like, “why bother at all?” Did Belle need a more fleshed out mother backstory? Most assuredly not. Did Lilo and Stitch need to be remade? Did the filmmakers have any unique takes or spin on the original? If they did, they didn’t make it to the final product.

It’s been more than a decade since I’ve seen the first movie, but so many scenes still stick with me to this day. One in particular that they dropped from the new cash-grab was Lilo getting to keep Stitch because she kept her receipt and the Galactic Empire respects property ownership above safety. I loved how silly and kooky it was, and it let Lilo standup for herself and Stitch one more time. Instead, they took the extra time to delve deeper into child protective services, which felt… odd. Particularly in a country with a history of separating indigenous children from their families, this was a weird choice for a movie that purports to be about no one being left behind. Of all the things to change, did Nani really need a love of marine biology to tell a story of her and her sister finding family out of the loss of their nuclear one?

I also missed the commentary that the animated movie had on white people in Hawaii - it felt like that was a movie with something to say. Whereas this remake only had something to be earned (money). You could feel that this movie had been defanged and had its edges shaved off. Yawn.

Every person in the crew is invincible, they all know martial arts, and that all lets the set pieces blossom into the most ridiculous spectacles you’ve ever seen. Balanced out with some very mid storylines and filled with meh dialogue, it’s all about family, and it’s gonna end with a Corona-ful family barbecue. You gotta love it.

As it turns out, because I started watching these movies at the 8th chapter, I began with the legend of a missing character named Brian. Through 8, 9, 10, and Hobbs and Shaw, no Brian (as Paul Walker had passed). Then I jumped back to the start and got to actually meet Brian and learn that he was originally the main character. So I accidentally totally get why George Lucas created Star Wars this way.
Finally, Fast Five remains the best one.
First one where they absolutely nailed the F&F ending, where everyone’s at the cookout drinking Coronas (with the labels out, of course).

The final Justin Lin movie of the series, and he still can’t direct fast action. That being said, he’s finally got the exciting, big, car-filled action set piece down. The tank scene wasn’t quite as strong as the bank vault one, but it sufficed.
Lastly, when you put Gina Carano next to Gal Gadot, Gal looks like Meryl Streep. Not at all salty that we won’t be seeing more Gina in this franchise.

An extremely solid follow up to the excellent first film. This series is so Chinese, I do wonder how much it’ll translate to a US audience. You do get a few extra jokes by knowing Chinese, in the same way that they sneak adult jokes into kid’s movies.
Having watched both dubs this week, I felt that the first one was dubbed a bit better, even if this cast could pronounce the borrowed Mandarin words/names a bit better.

It would be wonderful if Ne Zha unlocked more US wide distribution for Chinese movies, in the way that Disney distributing Spirited Away did for Japanese Movies / Miyazaki, but I’m not holding my breath.

This was so much better of an action movie than any of the preceding ones. They finally understood that all of the action didn’t need to be car-based, and they included a great ending action scene (the safe chase). Unfortunately the fast action still has an edit a second, and a ton of shaky cam.

And, this was a better F&F movie than any of the first four. This was about family, and they finally figured out that we wanna see everyone together, having fun and drinking beers. Gal Gadot (the weakest part of the last one) was way better here, and The Rock was a good addition to the franchise.
There are a few characters that speak Spanish consistently, and a few other non-English languages briefly spoken, mainly Portuguese, and nearly all of it has subtitles.

At this point of the marathon, I’m ready to say that I don’t love how Justin Lin directs action; he needs steadier camerawork. It was refreshing to have both Paul Walker and Vin Diesel back, but I didn’t really need the addition of Gal Gadot. Anyways, this was the closest movie to a modern F&F movie so far - they’re just missing the manic fun and the giant set pieces.
There were a few Spanish lines said across a couple of scenes, and they nearly all had subtitles.

paragraphs: This one is the most different of the set (that I’ve seen so far in my strange machete order viewing). Also, this movie exists in a world where drifting cars is the coolest thing that you could possibly do.

Most of the formula was here (the cars, the job, a notable car stunt, attractive women, Ludacris, and the overt masculinity), but where was Vin? This felt like about half of an F&F (in its full modern form), and that left me wanting for more.
What this movie does have is one of the best naming conventions of all time. The name 2 Fast 2 Furious will outlast any second of the actual footage.

Gavin Maddox Bergman was the best part of this movie, closely followed by Halsey. This was a bit funnier than I was expecting.

A pretty basic story told in the footprint of E.T., How to Train Your Dragon, and other stories where a strange or adversarial creature becomes a beloved pet and humanity demonstrator. It had enough heart to carry the story, but it really didn’t add much substance.
This one most likely won’t be staying with me for too long.

In 2017, I was given a personal, behind-the-scenes tour of Pixar’s Emeryville, CA offices from a friend who worked there (who was later laid off), and I can’t describe how cool the offices were. It’s the big, glass office they show when announcing the Monsters, Inc. box office. The (unshown) desk area included a crashed plane, a jungle set…etc. - all built by staff, and serving as functional desk and office spaces; it was like no other (tech) office I’ve visited - or even heard of - since. I think about that place a lot, how much those folks were devoted to their jobs and their craft.

This doc shows how much the Pixar folks invented computer animation as an art (and a science), and how quickly they mastered it. Yes, it’s a bit awkward for Lasseter to be so lauded (though this is old enough that he may not have been as creepy then), but it’s so nice to see fresh Steve Jobs clips again.

It worth watching if you like SNL, but it wasn’t incredible. I wish they’d gotten more of the stars, especially the remaining living originals.

reviews.filmTitle: Slave Play. Not a Movie. A Play.
paragraphs: I’m not sure if Slave Play (the play itself) was for me, and this doc tried to give as much of an appreciation for the work as it could, but it just didn’t personally click / coalesce.

I actually think I would’ve enjoyed this more if it were a showing of the play (a la Hamilton), or as an accompanying piece to seeing the play itself. It didn’t work as well as a standalone doc, trying to accomplish both of those at once.
Short, sweet, and right to the point, some of Wes Anderson’s best.
How either woman fell for Clive Owen’s character befuddles me
A really solid miniseries about the Utah War. It’s always nice when movies/TV feature less shown periods of US History, as opposed to just redoing the big wars over and over again.

You get two stories here: first, the story of a family escaping conflict traveling west, and how they (oh so lightly) intersect with the brewing Utah War with Brigham Young’s Mormons fighting the US Army. I really cared for the Mormon battle portion more than the family side, and ultimately would’ve been happier if they cut the settler portions (however well acted they might’ve been).
Meh. The only cool bit was the “wolfvision”

Watched this after Ends, which was my favorite bit of stand up in the last few years, just truly special. While Dots wasn’t quite that, there were sparks of his brilliance (telling moving, generational family stories) glowing here.
I’m pumped to see Ahir’s next set, whatever it may be about.
This was a lot funnier than I was expecting and had a good amount of heart.
The twists and turns were a bit too extreme for me. But for that, I had a really good time with A Different Man, and can see an argument for Sebastian Stan winning the Globe.
Oddly enough, this, Emilia Perez, and The Substance would make a good film series.
Some quality Wick. Having seen 4 already, the beginning of that movie now makes a bit more sense.

I’m fairly mixed on this one, because while I found Julianne Moore and Tilda Swinton great, I really didn’t like either Tilda or John Turturro’s characters. Also, while movie was directed quite well, I had a number of issues with the script, which had both cringey parts and some horrible exposition dumps.
In terms of the story and material itself, The Room Next Door tackles a challenging subject well. It’s bullshit that suicide is illegal

It’s hard to think of a protagonist that you root for more than Erin. Sometime you need to trust your gut and find a way to get a job you’re wholly un(der)qualified for, that you know in your heart of hearts you can do.
Bill and Ted has such a unique charm. It’s not great, but it’s pretty excellent.

In a movie full of great quotes, my favorite two were
“But Biiiill, those are historical babes”
“Bob Genghis Khan”
Robbie’s movie, much like his music, was really quite good. It’s a shame that America has failed to embrace either.
My main criticism is surprisingly that the movie needed more Robbie Williams music. Ideally there would’ve been a couple more songs included (and not just the instrumentals as underscoring).
Only watched + rated to complete a Letterboxd “collection”. Why do I care about these things?
Jeff Goldblum’s a treasure.
Short and bittersweet, an incredible artist gone too soon. No one makes beats like Avicii did.
There’s some footage cut in here, some was the same as the Netflix doc, and some was in Swedish with subtitles.
Decent documentary about a brilliant talent gone too soon. It’s impressive how much of this is told in Tim’s own voice.
The doc’s maybe ½ in Swedish, as most of Avicii’s friends and family are only shown speaking Swedish.
This documentary was weirdly split into two parts by Netflix, no clue why they’d do that to 90min content other than the data saying this ups watch time.

The most upset that you see Jerry getting at any point in the show’s history is when people are accusing him of faking the stories on a show built on further exploiting and embarrassing unwitting poor people from rural America. “How dare you accuse me of faking this exploitation porn!!” Tells you everything you need to know about the man.

And to the producer at the end who really said, “without us you wouldn’t have anything to watch”, I’m certain Netflix could’ve purchased or produced any number of more interesting stories than this dry and unchallenging retelling of a Wikipedia page. Maybe there’s some delightful, old Danish show that educated kids for decades that I won’t get to learn about because they made a show about the worst Jerry to come out of the 90s.
I loved all of the Philadelphia porn, but didn’t love the story that they told. That being said, Adrien Brody was excellent.
Is László Tóth the new Lydia Tar? Can we all pretend he’s real?
About a quarter of the spoken dialogue is in a non-English language with subtitles.

This was pretty good despite the camerawork, I did not need all of the shaky cam during fairly static shots. That being said, Pam, Billie, and Jamie (Lee?) gave some excellent performances and carried the film on their backs.
It was also nice to see Brenda Song in something again!
Why isn’t Mater respected among his people, like a doctor? Because ignorant people (cars) can’t see past his country accent, or broad stupidity.

He’s got some very specific knowledge (almost akin to being a doctor), and I’m ok with them devoting a movie to showing that, and that you should love your weird and eccentric friend. Sure it’s too much Mater, but I will defend that this movie is mid, not bad.
A sweeping epic, to be certain. It was strange how much English was spoken. If this were made today, I assume it would’ve been made in Mandarin.
Quality Cunk, I’ve just always wished that I found the bit funnier.
This movie was extremely prescient. Don’t connect your toaster to the home wifi!!
While I’m always going to root for some named Mookie wearing a Dodgers uniform, Mookie is an awful pizza delivery guy. That being said, this movie was great.

Nickel Boys is a lot, it’s beautiful, it’s heavy, it’s got incredible performances, and it’s shot creatively as hell (switching between two characters’ 1st person narration). At times, RaMell’s direction tops any other 2024 flick, and at other times the styling was too abstract and made the narrative a bit harder to follow.
I would be happy if this won Best Picture, or Best Director, it certainly deserves nominations for both (and maybe Screenplay as well).

A truly impressive 5 year documentary watching two young basketball players grow through high school. It’s impressive how the subjects progress and it’s accidentally poetic how each one’s story mirrors the other.
Truly a must watch of the documentary genre.
For what this was (a Super Bowl half time show, but in the middle of the season), it did a pretty darn good job, though I like Beyoncé and her new country music.
This was an extremely beautiful story, told in a super quick 50mins. It did leave me wanting more, but maybe that’s on me, I’m not used to self-contained media of this size.
They didn’t even play a little bit of the Bridgit Mendler song

If you’ve seen the trailer for this one, you’ve seen the full story. While The Fire Inside may be devoid of surprises, it isn’t lacking in the heart department. This feel-good story hits all of the notes that a well made sports biopic can do so well. When you add a fantastic Brian Tyree Henry performance, you get a quite good film. I really enjoyed this one.
Oh the emotional roller coaster that this one takes you on. You end up feeling so badly for Matt as Pepe is Nazified, but that’s thankfully not the end!
The story of the Taliban’s return to power in Afghanistan, as told through women activist’s eyes, as they lose autonomy in society.
The weakest part of this was the dialogue. I enjoyed the whole ensemble cast and the direction a decent amount.
RIP Angus King. I wonder if his role was affected by his untimely passing.
This wasn’t very jump scary, there were one or two in the beginning of the film, and it wasn’t very scary generally; it was far more gory than horrific.
A decent bit of horror, though a bit slow to start.
Not scary, more suspenseful.

Going through all of the Oscar likelies, and this was just the most meh. I’m tired of doing WWII flicks, especially when they’re about a lady who ignored people saying she didn’t belong, culminating bathing in Hilter’s tub.
Winslet was good, not in my Top 5 performances, but I wouldn’t be furious if she were nominated.
A fun body-swapping thriller, but I do wish they did more with the premise. That said. coda was a sufficiently satisfying resolution.

I’m not sure what I was supposed to take away from this, but as the owner of a cat who’s obsessed with sitting on my lap, the first few scenes of Nicole and Harris tumbling was eerily reminiscent of me telling Spark that he can’t sit on my lap.

reviews.filmTitle: Home Alone 2: Lost in New York
paragraphs: It’s impressive how much of the energy and beats of the original they were able to recapture while giving the movie a new, urban veneer. A very strong 3/5, and something I may revisit in Christmases future.

Robert Eggers’ Nosferatu was some really quality horror. More jump scares than I would’ve preferred, but a really haunting aesthetic throughout. The whole cast was excellent with Lily-Rose, Bill, Willem, and Simon McBurney as the standouts.
Maybe a hot take but, I really didn’t love the creature design of the vampire.
This was just on the outer perimeter of being funny
Oh man, they got Hasan in the controversy pic?
Everything Ryle does in this movie comes off so much worse in light of the lawsuit. Any veil of romance that it had is gone and this is just an uncomfortable thriller now.

reviews.filmTitle: A Saturday Night Live Christmas Special
paragraphs: This was just a clip show with no new footage whatsoever. Across the 50 years, there was enough quality content to populate an 85 minute special.
The clip show was an exercise in realizing, “oh that person overlapped with that other person”.
A serviceable Grinch movie, pretty glad it wasn’t mine growing up. The dog was cute and not overused.
I grew up on this movie, it’s such a classic, and that’s thanks largely to Jim Carrey, who is an outstanding Grinch, and Ron Howard’s vision.
The combination of Richard Linklater, Ethan Hawke, and the passage of time does seem to yield some magical results.
It’s appropriately been a long time since I’ve seen the first one, so I too was experiencing the passage of time and trying to remember what happened that night.
As someone that’s traveled the world for the last decade, it’s a bit strange that each of them had this strong, singular, lasting connection, but I guess that’s love.

Technically, this was well put together, but it really wasn’t for me and it felt quite flat. I really did like Angelina’s performance until they showed the credit archival footage of Maria, who had a lightness and warmth that just wasn’t in the film. I was really surprised by how different the two women seemed.

The sequel / prequel to the live action Lion King remake. And when they inevitably announce Lion King 2, it’ll have been my fault for seeing this. More notable than the uninspired film were the trailers for the live action Lilo and Stitch and How to Train Your Dragon which played before.
This is the state of Hollywood in 2024, and it’ll stay this way if we keep giving the positive affirmation of our box office dollars.

What can I say about this movie? Now I know:
- How Rafiki got his stick
- Why Mufasa was the king of all animals
- Why Pride Rock has its signature look
- How Mufasa met Zazu
- How Scar got his scar and nickname

Did I want to know any of this? Nope, of course not. The Lion King sequel portion was worse than the prequel majority, as Timon and Pumbaa had overstayed their welcome in the first act but kept popping up throughout.
Ultimately, nothing here really stayed with me, certainly none of the music but the “bye bye” song, for largely the wrong reasons.
This really took a while to get going, but once it did it had a nice heart.
Nothing special here as, grinchy Ben Stiller finds a heart in the country, away from his heartless corporate city life, in raising his orphaned nephews.
The premise of the movie was dumb and the scenes ranged from awkward to boring. LiLo was fine.

When it comes to comedian that toe the line, Anthony did it masterfully here. Ten minutes of hilarious trans jokes where trans people aren’t the subject of the joke - it feels actually refreshingly clever.

I say this as the highest compliment, at times he verged on Mitch Hedberg quality one liners. I wish he’d made more jokes, and talked about the jokes he was making less. Regardless, it was a very funny special.

reviews.filmTitle: The Simpsons: O C'mon All Ye Faithful
paragraphs: It’s been a long time since I’ve watched The Simpsons, and whoa does everyone sound different from how I remember them.
The plot really didn’t do it for me, though I liked Lisa waxing about Buddhism. It’ll probably be another little while before I check in on this basically geriatric-aged series.
This series is Fast & Furious for slightly younger kids, and people who grew up on the games or cartoons. I hope we get 10 of these.

Timmy could do it all: sing, play guitar, play harmonica, but the one skill that he didn’t pick up was motorcycle riding. The very few times that it was him on the bike, it was stationary, wobbly, or green screen.

Apart from that personal gripe of mine, this was a bunch of fun. Timothee is eminently watchable, and this movie leans very heavily into the music. A Complete Unknown will make you say, “I forgot Bob Dylan had so many bops”.
Also, as someone who recently stopped smoking cigarettes (again), this movie made me want a cigarette so badly.

reviews.filmTitle: Ronny Chieng: Love to Hate It
paragraphs: Hate to love it

reviews.filmTitle: Jamie Foxx: What Had Happened Was...
paragraphs: Emotional story of Jamie telling his near death incident in an almost church-like stage set.

reviews.filmTitle: George Harrison: Living in the Material World
paragraphs: A comprehensive documentary on George Harrison’s whole life. The best parts were psycho Phil Spector’s clips in his obvious wig, and Eric Clapton telling the tale of stealing George’s wife from him.
A fun watch for any Beatles fan; this reaffirmed my belief that George had the most interesting post-Beatle life.
I do like the presented narrative that celebrities are using James Corden as a free uber, and I like even more that he leaves in the first 4 minutes, to be replaced by Zane Lowe.

This is still the lowest effort, and least inspired, Christmas special that Apple TV could buy. It was nice to get to see some celebrity backstories, but yea, this is just for the Dua, Gaga, and Chappell fans; you get to see a bit of each of their personal lives. The only thing that nothing tops seeing Chappell’s parents, friends, and hometown is 15secs of Gaga singing Zeppelin.
“They call me The Foreigner because nobody knows where I’m from”

This was one of many horrible lines from Kraven a.k.a. The Hunter. Wow, this was such a stinker. The flashbacks were boring, the present day stuff was also boring. The Rhino was boring (when he wasn’t being accidentally funny), and Sergei and his family were boring. What a waste of a movie.
In aggregate, the Sony Marvel Spider-man Cinematic Universe was garbage.

Fortune’s funny, but this special is definitely for a certain type of people. There’s a bunch of jokes about interacting with her mom on Facebook, and I just couldn’t relate less, and that’s ok! A number of the other jokes landed with me.

reviews.filmTitle: A Nonsense Christmas with Sabrina Carpenter
paragraphs: The variety show is such a dated format, but Sabrina did a decent job with hers. That being said, the comedy didn’t really work, and the sexual innuendos didn’t quite do it for me, and they came frequently (wink). She does sing very well though
It feels like this would be such a loud experience
This has to be the first TSA movie that I’ve ever seen, and it wasn’t bad! I wouldn’t mind having Jason Bateman talking to me in my ear all day.
A beautiful story of perseverance and growth in the face of tragedy. I had no clue that he and Robin Williams were so close.

Wow, this one felt more political than ever coming out now. It really makes you think about the incentives and risks of journalism, while giving you a decent ride along the way. This is kind of what I was hoping to get with Civil War.
A really touching (unspoken) story of forced family, and how kindness pays forward. Basically the whole film is animals in peril, so if that’s not your cup of tea, you may want to skip this one.
The Wild Robot should win the animation Oscar, but Flow should certainly be nominated.
Probably my least favorite of Luca’s, though mostly not due to the direction.
All my favorite documentaries start with origin stories for how JFK Airport got its name.

So they had some decent Beatles footage. the issue was that they tried to add some narrative to hold the whole thing together. The footage worked, most of the rest of the interviews didn't. It was cool to hear from the living Beatles and the fellow musicians of the era, but they certainly could’ve nixed the “I have sex dreams about the dead Beatles” lady. Or maybe they didn’t have enough quality footage to use and padded it with empty fluff. Either way, liked the footage, didn’t like the edit.
To me, this will forever be the Disney movie that tried to teach kids that getting lost is a good thing.
What happened to shorts before Disney animated films?
I like James but just didn’t find this funny for the most part. I think/hope/guess it was rewarding for him.
One Guilty Man
(my 2,000th Letterboxd title logged!)
I don’t agree with all the additions, but Fiyero definitely needed that talking horse.

It’s remarkable that this cartoon, video game was able to be stretched into 90 minutes. It’s even more remarkable how genuinely funny it ended up being. This was such a trip, and reminiscent of Looney Tunes, and Tom and Jerry.
Make Rome Great Again!
A great lead performance and a few exciting action set pieces, but overall this movie felt kinda bland to me.
As a kid of Bridge to Terabithia, it was great to see AnnaSophia acting in more things!

This was good, but ironically I wish it was more of an operetta. Selena had a much larger arc in the second half, and didn’t sing at all during it! The story really didn’t go anywhere, but Zoe Saldaña gave an incredible performance, as did the other two leads.
>90% of the movie was in Spanish.
This was funny enough
As an amalgamation of the two leads, who would never go on a tour because of people like them, A Real Pain let me do some heavy self-reflecting. I’m certainly more Benji, sadly.
I enjoyed Jesse’s direction except for all the feet stuff. Way too many feet!
It was good, though it wasn’t really my cup of tea.
I had a good time with this, it was pithy and punchy. I’m excited to see what Anna Kendrick directs next.

reviews.filmTitle: Into the Fire: The Lost Daughter
paragraphs: There’s so many of these horrible people hiding among us. I’m just glad it’s harder to go on a murder spree and hide in the suburbs these days.
Just purely bad. One of those movies that thinks saying something louder is funnier. Don’t watch this one.
Pretty sure that I saw that house on Zillow

This was fascinating to see the precursor case to the OJ one, as I wasn’t born yet. Maybe the most fucked up bit was how society treated the boys’ sexual assault back in the 90s. That and the first prosecutor who was an absolute asshole.
Learned a lot of new/old Martha lore
I was shocked that this wasn’t an autobiographical film debut from a middle aged woman.
The stop motion was great, and the story was somehow even better (though really quite sad at times).
Really stunning visuals, with great writing and a decent story.
I appreciated that they never showed what anyone was looking it. It was more satisfying to learn about it through the dialogue.
Yea, this was decent enough. Some good chuckles here and there. Seth is watchable enough to hold you for the hour.

reviews.filmTitle: Hasan Minhaj: Off with His Head
paragraphs: I really appreciate this more unleashed energy. With this being in the Bay, there’s a decent chance that I knew someone in the audience.
This was such a blast and a whirlwind of a time. Anora left me feeling so satisfied in the end, like I got to experience a whole journey.
I’m currently studying Russian, having been to Armenia last month, so this film connected to me on a few Eastern levels in addition to being a smash.
Very mid finale to the Venom story. So little of the action was discernible, but the talking scenes were definitely worse than the action ones.

Across all three movies the best part was the Eddie/Venom relationship, and of course Vernon horse gets a shoutout. Unfortunately there were a bunch of lows, including the Venom crew, every military scene, and the weird villain.
Hated how they made stage managers the butt of the joke and a goof. The rest of the movie was pretty mid, but I really hated how they portrayed stage managers.
A beautiful movie, both visually and emotionally, about finding your place in life and who you belong with. Lupita was great
Dreamworks really has been on a roll as of late.
If you liked Smile, you’re going to like Smile 2. It has a lot of the same fun as the first one, and pushes the envelope in a few ways.
I’ll repeat, way too many jump scares! And this needed more scenes with Voss water, the real protagonist of the movie.
Fosters Home for Imaginary Friends walked so this movie could kinda stumble around for a bit. They even took the name Blue!
It sure did look pretty, but it just felt really flat, and I really don’t love the mixed animation style (Sonic gets a pass).
Not Ali’s best, but it still gave me a chuckle or two

I’m so glad that I started watching horror because of films like this. This was such a fun mix of body horror with a satire about women aging in hollywood while retaining a decent amount of levity and humor.
Fully reinforced my original belief that chimps shouldn’t be household pets. At least this time it was far clearer than Tonia was the villain than Joe was in Tiger King.
It’s a pretty straightforward musician’s biopic, though this one was undeniably told in the artist’s prefer style.
Pharrell has synesthesia and there’s a ton of wild colors shown around music. I do wonder how nice this movie looks with the synesthesia, and if Pharrell ensured the colors matched the music.

My entire audience was kids, but this certainly isn’t a kid’s movie. I think it’s quite a mismatch as kids aren’t going to react to seeing Busta or Gwen Stefani or hearing Hella Good. A fine movie, but a total marketing mixup.
This was semi-informative, and who knows, maybe they did finger the right guy.
The Trumpification of the Donald
A story of intergenerational trauma and forgiveness. While it takes some fairly extreme events to force people to change, overall the story was really strong.
I saw this on a blind “Unseen” screening, and the film name isn’t shown until the very end of the film, so I was extremely blind on this one.
Such incredible character design, and a truly great psychological horror where anyone could be the Thing.
The love story itself was quite nice as it explored a full lifetime’s worth of heartbreaks and joys. However the choppy format felt a bit tired.
Andrew and Florence were both great, though both have a bit of an ageless youth look as they barely age across the depicted decade.
It’s the Lorne Michaels show and his life is stressful, but Lorne is always able to remain calm and composed and clear eyed for the next 59 years.

I had an ok enough time with this. The jokes were funny. The calamity was arranged such that you get to see a bit of each portion, like a pu pu platter of skits. The cast was fun enough. It just felt very empty when you got to the end, the whole thing is a forgone conclusion (much like Air), so the stakes are vapor and the predictions feel hollow.
Dylan O’Brien’s Aykroyd was the most fun, closely followed by Cory Michael Smith’s Chevy Chase.
I guess you need to make Joker a political figure because otherwise there’s no story, but it still made no sense. The only politics he seems to have is violence is good.
anyways, I look forward to some high school putting on a production of Joker 2 in a few years.
This just like, didn’t do it for me.
One of the two gruff, serious guys should’ve been cooky. Give me The Nice Guys Ryan Gosling energy, or Brad Pitt in Burn After Reading wackiness.
I went into this show with nearly no expectations, and while not loving where the show began, it made sense from where they left the character.
I’m very much bought in and excited to see where the series goes! It’s not incredible so far, but I’m pleasantly surprised how much horror they’ve managed to sprinkle in so far.
This one ended up being deeply resonant to my life at three major points. I do love when a movie can do that while still being funny.
If you can only see Aubrey Plaza in one movie this weekend, make sure it’s this one.
No.

Such an incredible special that really only Ahir could’ve told, despite aspects of the story being true to thousands of people. The storytelling trumps the comedy at multiple points, and that was a-okay with me.
I welled up a few times, maybe it was the plane, but definitely it was Ahir and the heart of it all.

I love Nickelback, I’ve always loved Nickelback. I like modern Nickelback, and I like old Nickelback. But this really wasn’t a great documentary, the band themselves are fairly boring, in a quite Canadian way.
Also, this needed more Avril. There was more Billie Joe Armstrong and Ryan Reynolds in this than Avril Lavigne.
This was a sweet watch, but it just didn’t quite resonate with me to the degree that I hoped it did. Maybe it’s because most of my family holidays ended in yelling and tears, a me-issue.

Pretty simple horror, but quite effective. My main complaints were it felt a bit slow in a few places, and relied way too heavily on jump scares. I’m probably still going to watch the sequel in theatres.

Well, this was definitely not a “fun” watch. I went into this blind and was expecting something funny or at least with a bit of levity. Instead you get a lot of sulking and depressed Sennott, dealing with life, death, and people acting their worst. Like an even darker and more dour Funny People.
It was good, elevated by Rachel’s performance, but it was a lot for a plane watch.
But for Wednesday, better Burton than we’ve had in a while. It was a fun ride with a great Elfman score. The women shonee
Of course a Safdie directed this. This is old Sandman somewhere near his best. It’s weird, and it’s eccentric. Some of the bits may be real, but it doesn’t really matter that they likely aren’t.
Sandler shines the brighest when he’s being musical.
I’ve definitely seen way too many murder docs, but this felt very straightforward and flat. Very skippable

Wow, what a weird movie. The whole thing is set from a 2020s Russian POV, and everything is narrated by these Soviet sympathizers fawning over how great Reagan was. Jon Voight, in a not great Russian accent, excuses away Iran Contra as “the lifeguard was just trying to bring his people home”. Aids is never mentioned.
The script started from a place of lionizing the former president, and brushing everything away that doesn’t fit into the narrative. You don’t need to see this movie.
Caught this on a mystery prerelease screening, and was pretty hyped when I discovered I’d be watching Slingshot.

That slowly dissolved over the course of the movie, until they immediately snatched me back all at once. They seriously landed the plane, despite some turbulence throughout (pun slightly intended). The writer of Moon wrote this, which makes a lot of sense.
When the credits rolled, I was pretty damn satisfied with Slingshot, though I don’t know if this one will stay with me.
Before the hacking (and the internet) was depicted as a bunch of wacky 90s tubes or Matrix code falling, it actually looked like a Terminal window. Go figure.
That dinner scene evoked most of my family holiday dinners perfectly.
I really wanted to love this but it felt like less than the sum of its parts. Robert Smigel should be my rabbi.
This was a 1/5 movie with a singular 3/5 scene, but the dialogue was so consistently bad that I’m not giving it any higher than a 1

This is the spiritual successor to Get Out in so many ways, certainly including this being an extremely strong directorial debut. I loved the usage of colors and sounds, and this may be the best vaping appearance in cinema history.

It bears stating that this is an extremely dark movie, with a slightly more realistic plot than many thriller, mystery horrors choose to. Accordingly, there’s a trigger warning that runs before the film. It won’t be for everyone, but it was definitely for me.
This has a modicum of Dark Knight energy, where The Crow is both The Joker and Batman, and Bruce Wayne is dead. It’s not nearly as good, but it evokes the latter movie in a few places.
This was really enjoyable, despite the overarching tragedy of watching Brandon’s final work.
Tried to see this opening night in IMAX but the projector broke. I think the universe was trying to save me, but I didn’t heed its warning.
As someone who has never played the game(s?) before, this didn’t make me want to play them.

This movie taught me that Italians pronounce Cecila almost like Chinchilla, and that was pretty cool. It started quite meh and never really elevated from there. Sydney Sweeney wasn’t amazing, but she was there the whole time.
Maybe 20% of the movie is in Italian, and some have subtitles, some is translated to us, and Sydney. We don’t get to hear Syd speak much Italian at all.
Patrick Swayze had some Homelander vibes

Best Alien since Aliens. They stole everything from the original Alien that worked, including the fantastic character design. Cailee Spaeny was an excellent final girl, and sold every dumb decision that her character made.
I will say that this is a movie that would be enhanced with a subtitled viewing, as a few characters have British accents, and all seem to be the mumbly kind.
I guess Matt, Ben, and Apple decided that Casey’s out of sex offender Hollywood jail and ready to star in the pictures again. The people crave Casey’s Bostonian accent, we must sate the masses!

It’s a heist movie where the heist goes wrong in about a dozen ways, and it’s perfectly fine. It’s also filled to the brim with famous people; they even managed to squeeze Jack Harlow into this thing. Matt Damon’s never been dumber, and it’s not quite believable.
The standouts are the perpetually angry and paranoid Michael Stuhlbarg, and the plot point that Boston has been run by a corrupt and borderline fascist mayor for decades.

reviews.filmTitle: Matt Rife: Lucid - A Crowd Work Special
paragraphs: This man was very charming and funny, but I did have an overwhelming sense that I could do that
I saw this on a blind prerelease screening and it was fine. The story was nothing I hadn’t seen before (and I successfully guessed a twist in Act One).
Though there were some tonal inconsistencies and I didn’t love Elizabeth Banks’ direction (albeit she had some cool shots), I thought she gave a really good leading performance.
Trippier Thelma & Louise (probably more accurately Bonnie and Clyde, but I haven’t seen that yet).

This movie wants to say something about the American fascination with real crime, which has only gotten more intense in the last 30 years, but it just gets lost in the “killing cool” narrative ultimately - not surprised this was a Tarantino story.
RDJ was doing an early Tropic Thunder, and Tommy Lee Jones was zanier than I’ve ever seen him be before, he may as well have been animated as those trippy cartoon segments.
This was one crazy story, but in the end, a lot more of it worked than didn’t. Hunter Schafer was a great final girl and Dan Stevens was very creepy but not all that German.
This was a strange movie, the bulk of it is based in “modern day” with an aged Thatcher being (mostly lovingly) haunted by her dead husband.
Anyways, it would take a lot to make me enjoy a Thatcher biopic, it’s tough not to roll my eyes at the girl boss posturing as she’s attacking unions. Regardless, Meryl was great as always.

The direction of this movie was so flat, it needed a lot more dynamic musical underscoring, that and more interesting writing, or faster pacing. It just ended up being a bit of a drag from the production.
Billie, Gillian, and especially Rufus were all pretty great.
It’s hard to think of how a movie could represent my formative years more perfectly than Didi’s lonely SmarterChild conversation.
Nice short little doc for a nice short little man

Such an incredibly important documentary, as you watch two reporters capture the beginning of the Ukrainian War. Morally, I’m with the doctor who led the reporters into the operating room to document the mass civilian deaths. This was history and it needed to be captured.
The documentary has an haunting narration in English, while much of the footage shown is spoken in Ukrainian, approximately 30% of the language has subtitles.
Lady Raven stan and day one.
This was the right amount of dumb fun. Is Shyamalan back in a peak era? Josh Hartnett was extremely watchable, I’d watch another one of these.
I was constantly confused what Eddie was competing for, but I just don’t understand ski jumping as a sport. This was a fairly straightforward biopic with some pretty good Taron and Hugh performances.
I only got halfway through this movie before falling asleep last night (that’s on me), but the whole weather thing really wasn’t doing it for me. I may finish this one day, or not.
At multiple points, I found myself wanting to shout “shut up about the sun” like a sleepy but frustrated Andy Bernard.
This ended up being a pretty solid Alien movie. It was at its worst when David was onscreen, and its best when a Xenomorph was onscreen.
Michael Fassbender says “mother” like Buster Bluth.
Terrible script
I didn’t need the romance plotline, the rest of the movie was unimpeachable.

reviews.filmTitle: Dirty Pop: The Boy Band Scam
paragraphs: I went into this disliking Lou, and left this disliking him significantly more. If you’re worried that they sugarcoat his life story, they really don’t.
You get (what feels like) a fairly balanced perspective from Lou’s friends and the people who he screwed, including some very famous ones.

I went to the premiere of this at 7pm in IMAX, with various people in Deadpool costumes, applause at the Marvel logo, screams at every character introduction, and laughter at every joke. Peak Marvel viewing conditions, and still meh. The weakest part was definitely the writing.

Admittedly this had some great music from my childhood but it just felt really tired - even joking about being in lull couldn’t save the movie from failing in the same ways as the rest of the 2020s MCU.
spoilerParagraphs: As a Fox Marvel send off, this felt fitting. Some high highs, and a lot of meh to sit through. I didn’t need all the Logan fawning. It was good, I saw it, we get it.

When Happy says “aim for the middle and you’ll never miss” that was accidentally the most meta line of the movie. That’s been Disney’s corporate strategy for the last few years and they’ve missed left and right, and still can’t seem to figure it out.

paragraphs: What an absolutely wicked, narcissistic man that created a massive incest risk. It was a decent documentary but I was confused about when “now” was at a few points.

I LOVED Kneecap which managed to be extremely overtly political and funny at the same time. The main actors weren’t incredible, but they were certainly charming and humorous enough to carry the movie.

Oddly enough, as someone who’s spent a bit of time in the “North of Ireland”, and only a few days in the Republic of Ireland, Georgia’s accent was harder to understand than any of the Northern Irish accents. If you’re new to both accents, this film may be a bit tough to understand.
About half of the film had subtitles.
This was very strange
This was a great level of fun-stupid. The plan was absolutely terrible, and the science was all gobbledegook; and honestly that made the dry script way funnier, whether intentional or not.
At one point the protagonists get a 3D scan of the tornado for the first time, and the scientific genius screams, “our moisture levels were off!” You gotta love an accidentally funny script.
Damn this was one of the quietest movies I’ve ever seen. The camera was also wobbly as hell.

Apart from that, this was a really touching depiction of finding hope in a hopeless place. Colman was especially good, even for himself. He gives an excellent locked up “theatre kid” at the beginning.
One of the many great Philip Seymour Hoffman performances, and somehow, out of 1900 films, my first Helen Hunt movie.
I don’t mean this to be insulting, but I don’t think Luc Besson knows what a brain is.
The best queer cowboy movie since Brokeback.
Loved this story about finding your people and finding yourself!
The full George Carlin story, told primarily in his own voice and through his work. The first part was better than the second, but the whole thing was excellent and well worth a watch.
Deeply unnerving. I’ve never been more glad to have been born on the 15th.
Whichever Apatow sang Memory killed it
I didn’t know the AMC Theatres commercial lady made movies. She wasn’t awful, unfortunately, this movie was

reviews.filmTitle: Back to the Future Part III
paragraphs: If this film was made today, there’s no way that they’d depict the actual, real world, gun control measures of the wild west in the 1800s.

reviews.filmTitle: Back to the Future Part II
paragraphs: I love how there’s always the perfect newspaper headline to provide exposition on what’s happening, or what happened in the past. Also it’s convenient that Biff doesn’t fuck with the free press in his (seemingly) absolute power.

This was really heartbreaking at times to watch, and really inspirational at other times. Celine is so raw and shows you her personal struggles as she’s lost her ability to sing and even at times walk, but she keeps relentlessly pushing through. As great as Celine is, the doc does feel a bit unfocused at times, and seems to get distracted a lot.
Also, as someone who’s outgrown three shoe racks now, I NEED Celine’s motorized, rotating shoe wall.
This was a fun, cute little moon rom-com. Nothing spectacular, but some solid writing and ScarJo was great as always.
Between this and A Quiet Place, lots of cats in 2024 movies.

I’ve never seen an animated movie with so many framing issues. There was an obese character who never once fit on screen, and frequently Gru’s head would move out of the shot. So very strange, and speaks to the poor direction.
I get that Gru being older means that they needed to use 80s references, but honestly who were they for? Me, most likely. Young kids these days have parents with 90s nostalgia.
I’m pretty sure the LAPD had a higher body count than the serial killer
This was a really sweet and touching tribute to the last 60+ years of LGTBQ comedians, which was largely led by lesbians.
And of course, an eternal fuck you to Anita Bryant.
Manifest Destiny Part 1
Wow, this thing didn’t know how to end. Because it kept going and introducing more characters, it had something of a Fellowship of the Ring vibe, in that sense.

By far the most interesting thing about this movie was the politics, which were comfortably right wing, with flourishes of “racism is bad” but only in the extreme contexts like scalping and active genocide. The film just completely excuses manifest destiny as a fait accompli, as “people are just going to keep moving west”. If you’re looking for them to unpack anything serious about America’s westward expansion, this isn’t the film for it. Also, the liberal stand-in characters were so funny and incompetent.
A woman and her cat go to get a pizza when some wacky hijinks ensue
This was a lot: a lot of good, and a lot of excess. All-in-all, I think the series of hour-long stories worked.
Figured I’d watch this before Deadpool & Wolverine, and to see my final X-men film. For others inspired to do the same, happy to report that this one is entirely skippable.
After having watched Shogun, it was funny to see Hiroyuki Sanada having a close relationship with a character called Mariko.
A wonderfully cute with a smidge of nonagenarian thrills that didn’t fully click for me.
The B-story lines were never great, despite having an excellent cast; it felt like it was less than the sum of its parts in the end.
The inciting incident of this film, and its resolution, were both terribly dumb, the rest of the movie was pretty fun.
I bet a lot of weird old men have countdowns to the princess’ 21st birthday.
Alexander Payne just gets life, man, and Giamatti’s always great.

As someone who wasn’t alive when the Brat Pack was relevant, there was no nostalgia value here for me. I think the project works because it comes from a place of genuine curiosity from Andrew, the director and lead subject, but it falters from the same thing. In the end, what you’re left with in the end is Andrew’s insecurities, which really isn’t enough to tie the thing together.
I was appreciative that this was a documentary and not a 4-part docuseries.
My god this was boring. The fact that the same director made this and Kick-Ass is a testament to how people can improve in their careers.
Fun setting and subject but the story went nowhere and didn’t have much to say. Tom Hardy was doing his Marlon Brando and Jodie Comer’s never been more midwestern.
A really good directorial debut, though noir’s certainly aren’t my genre. You can really see the foundations for what would later become Knives Out here a decade prior.
A sweet tale of a man who likes to punch (and has some half decent reasons to be swinging) falling in love.
Kinda felt like PTA at his purist, in both good and bad ways.
In like 5 words Robot Dreams had so much to say about life and friendship.

This is set in a largely speechless Bojack world, where the humans have been fully bred out, human verbal languages included. But they fail to deal with the advanced species vs. feral species divide. The characters go fishing at one point, and have to deal with an ant infestation, with both being considered more food than friend. But crocodiles are able to run junk yards?!?
This one really wasn’t as deep as the first, and didn’t really break any new ground. I loved the first one, and this felt like a lesser copy.
Marry your gay lover while you can!

The through line of Linklater’s films is a lack of things happening. Even in this movie, where maybe the most things happen, it feels like things have quick and simple resolutions. Never change, Richard!

reviews.filmTitle: Dancing for the Devil: The 7M TikTok Cult
paragraphs: They made this documentary way too soon
Suzumi has some hard Kingdom Hearts vibes: you’re sticking keys into holes to save worlds, you got Keystones, I smell a lot of similarities.
Anyways, this’s was a beautiful looking film, and a decent-enough epic of a story.
I was not expecting this to be so prominently set in SF, or to be so funny.
A great performance and a pretty rough screenplay. If you like Amy’s music, you’ll get all the hits and some earlier tracks performed well enough.

I was going to say bad things about this movie, then they included the “milk steak” Sunny clip and all my complaints washed away. More movies need to include It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia clips in their runtimes.
This really didn’t work for me. It felt like a weird mishmash of Captain Planet, Star Wars, and a dozen other sci-fi flicks. Chris Tucker was in another movie.
An indisputable damnation of Dupont from thorough explanations of how they knowingly poisoned every single human being and animal on the planet.
Mark Ruffalo has played this role a few times now, and he kills it every time. Tim Robbins has never seemed taller than he does in one of the wide shots standing next to Mark.
Election is so horny, it keeps getting distracted from the school plots to phantasize about sex. And nothing’s more 90s than yelling “don’t vote” and getting thunderous applause.
This movie also has that 90s uncomfortable relationship with adult-child sexuality. They go out of the way to say acting on it is wrong, but in every other instance they lean into it.
Apart from that all, this was a really fun movie, I think I just like Alexander Payne’s writing and direction.
Why does every documentary come out as a mini-series today? I miss the age of the docufilm, where things were edited down; this one certainly could’ve been edited into a 90-100min format.
I’m kinda mixed on if this was good or not. It had a lot to say about a lot of things, but really failed to say much about any of them.

I would not recommend watching this after Furiosa, watch this one first. It’s impressive to see how far this series has evolved over the decades from one guy’s tinkering, and what through-lines have remained: lots of cars and bikes going vroom vroom. There’s a ton of really impressive car and bike shots for the era, you can tell how talented the director is his debut.

This was a lot of silly violent fun. Furiosa’s tragic story never gets too dark, and maintains at a fuel-injected clip. I was amazed how long we spent with young Furiosa, she got nearly half the film. While I do wish there was more action, I understand that you got a richer story with more character moments in the trade-off.
Both Furiosas were great, as was Tom Burke. Chris Hemsworth was doing a lot, and most of it worked.
An ode to chain-smoking cigarettes and dating your boss. They don’t make ‘em like this anymore.
In my head canon, Harvey personally requested the many butt shots.

Flo, the accent isn’t working for me. It’s not at all lived in, and really comes and goes. She’s a a good casting choice for everything but a non-London English accent. This was nice, it gives you the nice feels that you want.
This was a lot more fun than X, and has got me hyped for Maxxxine
This was seriously a lot. You watch one person go through a ton of harm (much of it self-inflicted), and not in a comedic way. This is good, but really not sure if I’d recommend it.
It’s wild to take a show which was on the air across the Bush administration, and not really an artifact of its time, and then revivify it extremely in the Trump presidency.
I did find the special humorous, but it’s quite a different show. There’s no Hanna-Barbera cameos or references, it’s all political analogs, very much of 2018.
I’m going to be returning to the series, not the special. If they make another special, I’d of course watch it.
Ah yes, a story of big bookstore crushing the little guy, set riiight before Amazon comes in and erases the entire industry (but ironically for the rare little bookstore).
I wish we’d bring back those 90s graphics, I love me some goofy, blocky animations! This 2hr AOL commercial was the perfect time box nostalgia trip.
Greg Kinnear is so relatable in this movie, I am Frank Navasky in too many ways. This movie would’ve been 3.5 stars if it ended 15mins earlier; Meg Ryan was way too slow here.

Just to start out, I’m so glad that they figured out that the two teams need different colors. This was great to watch as a back-to-back with Boys State, if only to even further accentuate the sexism between the programs. It’s sheer bullshit how much better Boys State was than Girls State. What was with all the singing, and “no showing your backs”?

Faith Glasgow and Cecilia Bartin can stump, damn. I think Emily’s a bit of a victim of her ideology, as she points out herself that her party doesn’t have a platform. The successful members of her party demagogues to get fealty and power, and Emily’s too soft to pull that off. I’m glad she got a redemptive third act.
I had no idea that Boys State existed until watching this documentary. It’s such a cool program, I’m glad that it exists. This is a great documentary.
spoilerParagraphs: It’s incredible how this mirrored modern politics. You had a Beto style candidate, beloved by a minority, who lost because he was perceived as being too anti-gun. Then the entire sleaze-ball strategy working so effectively that the mudslinging party swept. Also, Texans not being split ticket voters. They pick a party and go down ballot (in the majority).
Just like with Beto, I fell for Stephen and had my heart broken when he lost.

paragraphs: You think it’s just gonna be another classic Massachusetts lesbian escapade, but you get a bit more.
An incredible supporting role by Marin Ireland, wow.
This was more acting than I’ve seen The Rock do in the last five films, combined (and he basically just put on a NY accent, and acted old).

2manji  was an entirely superfluous and middling and tired and uninspired movie, the “body swap” gimmick was old in the first remake. More than a quarter of this movie was characters saying each other’s names.

When I caught the trailer for Babes, I said that I’d never see it. I never plan to have kids, and don’t love Ilana’s humor so this was never going to be for me. When I realized that my surprise early screening was Babes, I groaned.

All-in-all, this was fine. I almost left a few times, but stuck it out. If you find Ilana hilarious, this will definitely be for you. If not, you’re left with an educational flick that walks you through the earliest stages of motherhood.

reviews.filmTitle: The Jinx: The Life and Deaths of Robert Durst
paragraphs: If you told me “they’re making another season of The Jinx”, I’d say that HBO is running out of ideas, but I’ve been really impressed with how interesting and intriguing the trial has been. It was merited!
Bad accents and head bears, god this was awful
Dwight Schrute did it better, honestly.
Guy Ritchie has too much fun writing his racist-ass characters, and I was not vibing with his Princess Bride-inspired narration.
Hugh Grant has been in a renaissance since at least 2019.
Cool movie, I love Bruce Springsteen
“Karate at the King of Prussia mall”, M. always brings the local western Philly suburb references.
This was entirely too long, but I laughed more than I was expecting. Kevin Hart miraculously was the only good A-lister, and I loved his Quaker joke.

For basically every movie that I watch, my brain will produce a score for the film about 30mins in. The credits rolled before I had any clue what I thought about this movie, and I’m still really wrestling with how I felt about it.

The direction was really interesting, but I really disliked some shots. I enjoyed The Pink Opaque’s aesthetic and horror-stylings, probably more than the “real world”. The story had a lot of great parts, but I wasn’t sure about some parts of the story, and ultimately wasn’t sure about the ending. Though I really don’t love magical surrealism, I’ll admit this was it done well.
Also, I’ve never trusted the moon, and I appreciate that trepidation being affirmed.

reviews.filmTitle: My Next Guest with David Letterman and John Mulaney
paragraphs: This was a cute little pairing. This may’ve been at its best when Dave met John’s dad

reviews.filmTitle: Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes
paragraphs: This was great, these films always seem to say a lot of interesting things about humanity.
There were so many apes in enclosed spaces, and a lot of birds too, but no poop. I call bullshit, there’d be poop everywhere!

reviews.filmTitle: Star Wars: Tales of the Empire
paragraphs: So this was a twofer: Morgan was a 2.5 and Barriss was a 3.5.

I almost wish we got a standalone Barriss story and then it could’ve gone in its own direction and not had to be a foil to Morgan. I feel like Disney had some good new Star Wars here (albeit in the same damn time period as the rest of it all), and extended on the wrong aspects of it. That’s the Filoni curse.
This wasn’t so much scary as it was strange.

Wow, I love maximalist, millennium, Angelina Shakespeare. Baz Luhrmann takes the Bard’s original words and stylizes the set dressing to the max, and wow does it work. Creativity overflowths here. If I’m going to watch Shakespeare, this is a pretty digest form for the sometimes dry texts.
Feels like required viewing, supplemental to your middle school American history class. Also there’s a cop-hating horse
This was really good, I’m sad that I missed it in theatres. Greta nailed that ol’ timey metaness
I didn’t have Jerry Seinfeld writes and directs a furry January 6th scene on my 2024 bingo card.
For an action, comedy, romance this accomplished all three decently well but never really wowed me.
Jody’s film looks terrible. The worst of Mad Max, Dune, and a sweeping romance.
Felt both somewhat original and completely done before
Not since Inglorious Bastards has a film taken such a hard (correct) “all Nazis must die” stance, though they forgot the blood on this one. This was a PG-13 movie with a few fucks sprinkled in.
A bit strange to cast a Mexican as a half Jew, but that’s just me. Yea, this was fun, I’d watch it again on TBS.

This series really has been a roller coaster, at times its felt like a spy thriller, but overall it’s been somewhat mid. By the end, I just didn’t care about the characters or the story, this mini-series overstayed its welcome.
This movie had the ultimate challenge, make tennis not boring, and they definitely succeeded. Luca really tried to find every interesting camera shot, didn’t he
Strange and funny, but strange.
I was worried he couldn’t be funny without his blocks, but he could. Some of the better rape jokes that I’ve heard.
Very funny, but not entirely in a haha kinda way
This was pretty funny. More relatable if you’re an east coast Jew, but there might be something in it for you too
The most pacifist movie I’ve seen in a while. The movie has a point and it’s that war is hell. It’s not original, but it’s got a unique setting, nearly modern day America.

All four of the lead actors were great, but as with all his films, the star was Alex Garland’s heart-wrenching tension and pacing. The ending set piece had me at the edge of my seat for a good twenty minutes.
In a few areas, this film left me wanting more. With its heavy and powerful tone, it’ll be a minute before I’m ready to revisit Civil War. Also, I don’t want to risk tinnitus.
This was a good directorial debut, though it had way more shaky cam and too many edits during the action scenes.

This also wasn’t quite an action movie. It definitely had John Wick level violence and lack of bruises, but the action set pieces were a bit few and far between. It was a mix of a whole bunch of things, it was good, and it was a lot.
Any movie where the police are the enemy will get a kudos from me.
Wolfgang Halbig and Alex Jones seem to be competing to be the singular worst person in America.

I had no clue how ubiquitous Steve was in the last 70s. This was a great climb to fame for someone who really worked his way up. While part one was definitely stronger than part two, the whole documentary made me appreciate Steve Martin the person and the comedian so much more.
Batman v Superman in so many ways, but instead of Martha we get Mothra.
The plot doesn’t move without 60secs of exposition dumps or a deus ex machina.
I liked it! I could’ve done without all the body sounds, but hey, beggers can’t be choosers.

reviews.filmTitle: Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV
paragraphs: They say the fish rots from the head, and Dan Schneider is one rotten fish head.
I’m actually not surprised pedophilic men flocked to kid’s tv shows. That just like, makes sense to me. I blame Nickelodeon for not protecting the kids, basically the whole time.

reviews.filmTitle: Turning Point: The Bomb and the Cold War
paragraphs: A fairly comprehensive overview of the Cold War, from a very heavily American POV, focused most centrally on the nuclear powers. You will get a number of first hand stories from people who were at the events: from Hiroshima survivors to Bay of Pigs invaders.

The series starts with the fall of Hitler’s Germany and goes to the 2020s with the invasion of Ukraine. A really wide view on the conflict and its impacts on the world today. While there was nothing groundbreaking here, this was a really worthwhile, albeit long, watch.
If someone asks, “what happened during the Cold War”, and they have 12 spare hours, this is one of the better (simple) resources to recommend.

I saw Taylor’s Version (the Disney+ version), which was probably my preferred way of experiencing Taylor’s body of work tour. I appreciate sound mixers balancing the levels of scream-singing and scream-screaming.
All-in-all, this was a fun time, and it didn’t quite feel as long as it was (though I was doing things around the house and working a bit during it).

reviews.filmTitle: How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days
paragraphs: While the premises for getting these two to date are absolutely ridiculous, this is one of the better unromcom romcoms. The stars are great, this is some good fun and holds up decently well.

A damning indictment of so many aspects of America, not just our immigration system. Tilda Swinton was excellent as the worst woman in the world. I wanted this to be funnier, as I felt it nailed the heartfelt bits better than the humorous ones.
I’m waiting for someone to tongue the kung fu out of me

reviews.filmTitle: A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood
paragraphs: I didn’t grow up watching Mr. Rogers (but oddly walked by his studio all the time in Pittsburgh), so this was a bit strange to me. I don’t have the reverence for the man, that he most certainly merits, so I watched this movie as an outside observer. It never fully clicked with me, and I acknowledge that was likely a me thing.

The framing of having Mr. Rogers helping our protagonist was probably one of the better ways to tackle his story. Tom Hanks was fine, but kinda came off a bit creepy at time with his smiley face. I really didn’t care for, or connect with, Matthew Rhys or his family or story, sadly.

This show is absolutely phenomenal. The characters are so well rounded, and the story’s set at an interesting time period where I don’t know any of the characters or history. It’s almost like a historical House of the Dragon. They stick the landing so nicely, just a joy to watch.
About ½ of the dialogue is in English (well “Portuguese”, but it’s spoken in English) for the first few episodes, then it falls down to maybe ¼ or ⅓ English.

reviews.filmTitle: The Program: Cons, Cults, and Kidnapping
paragraphs: Wow, that was truly insidious. I can’t imagine profiting of child abuse like that, what a horrible family the Litchfields are.
Madame Web could never

I was really hesitant to see this movie, having just recently watched the original. I wasn’t sure I wanted to go through the heavy story again, especially when Spielberg’s movie holds up so well. I generally abhor this trend of remaking everything anyone’s ever heard of, so my distaste here has nothing to do with this specific film being sacred in my eyes.

Obviously this remake has that 21st century sheen that all the modern remakes have. That’s fine, I guess. When it comes to the story itself, they barely changed a beat. It looks different; it is the same. The major difference is the music, while the artists are all extremely talented, the music never stuck with me.

This was fine. Everyone did a great job, but I just didn’t really want or need this from the get go. I missed Whoopi’s humor, the remake wasn’t funny at all. I missed a lot of the depth of character built from Spielberg’s more subtle direction. When I want to revisit this story, I’m rewatching the 80’s version.

Oof this has some tonal issues. It’s really trying hard to be funny and like Veep at times, but the humor isn’t working. Then they do all the serious stuff, and that somehow also doesn’t work. They don’t really seem to be nailing anything yet.
Kate Winslet is giving it her best, but she’s working with next to nothing. One episode in, and I’m not sure if I’ll be watching a second.

I’m confused a bit how this show was produced. It’s designed for the smallest niche of people (probably including me, but likely me at 16). I guess the cost of making this one show is teeny compared to AWS’ profits, at Amazon scale.

It’s got almost exclusively a cast of Broadway stars and some great music, but the tone is really teenage. It feels like someone mashed together 6teen, Drawn Together, and Schmigadoon and doubled the usage of “fuck” and “cunt”, and made it more goth-y.
The writing is fine, and you can tell that they spent a lot more energy on the character design, as every character is a fully fleshed character in the aesthetic of the red/black/hearts style.
I’ll have to rewatch this, maybe on my Vision Pro… Incredibly beautiful film, with a fairly straightforward, slightly weird plot. This was a strong 8/10, maybe even a 9/10.
Some great acting from basically every A-lister, with a special shoutout for Javier Bardem, who made the whole theatre laugh a dozen times, or more.
Gimme Denis’ Dune Part 3!

reviews.filmTitle: Rory Scovel: Religion, Sex and a Few Things In Between
paragraphs: This was funny enough
Dude has an impeccable taste in music
This was fine
The best possible explanation for what was in the Pulp Fiction case. Equal parts fun and funny, with a great largely female cast.
It felt kinda Burn After Reading in some respects, with a 70s music video cut throughout, despite being set in the 90s.
This was a really cute kid’s film. If you have a child that’s afraid of the dark, this is the perfect movie for them. As an adult, it was charming and sweet, nothing extraordinary but a good time.
There’s absolutely nothing here that you haven’t seen in a dozen films before.
Objectively fine, but with plenty to dislike. Marisa Tomei’s accent was awful, the plot had the protagonist constantly using and lying to everyone.
Camila Mendes deserves her Charles Melton shot in a good film.
This was a fun and heartwarming story of a bunch of losers learning how to win. If you’ve seen the trailers, you’ve seen the movie.
I want Taika to take a big swing at something. This felt like a dinky little safe single.
On the precipice of Walking Hard, but Bob Marley had enough of a message and national redemptive arc to avoid making my list.

I enjoyed this, but will say that it was hard to understand the Jamaican English at times. Also they could’ve cut a good 10-15 mins out of the story. I loved how much music they put it, it really kept the film going.
I forgot Adam Scott was in this movie, twice.
Not quite so good it’s bad, but swinging that way on the pendulum. You could feel the rewrites in the story, which stumbled it’s way to the most basic plot of all time.
This was fun and campy and funny and weird. I didn’t love the dialogue but the writing still managed to be genuinely funny.
Kathryn Newton was excellent, Cole Sprouse was there. I loved every member of Lisa’s immediate family, her dad, her sister, and her mom were all solid-A characters.

Did this movie need to be made? No.
Was this movie fun to watch? At points.
Oh this is one of those child sexualization movies. Yea, it was fine; I appreciated all of the *NSYNC.

A visually beautiful, wish-fulfillment story carried by Andrew Scott’s performance. As a straight man with two living parents a lot of the harder hitting scenes didn’t personally affect me, but the story still hit some really strong emotional beats.
Terrifying story which starts off strong then gets sad and loses a bit of gas before ending on a positive note. I’ll likely forget about this story by the end of the week.
I realized about halfway through that my life was a perfect mixture of Robert and Fran. The movie was good, albeit dry and slow, and I think that was the point.
They played the new AI Beatles song about as much as Titanic did My Heart Will Go On. Apple’s really trying to get some cross-brand synergy out of that collaboration.

Oof this was not good. I don’t think this was written by Taylor Swift because I’m assuming she could produce better dialogue than this. The cat and action sequences were both terrible CGI, and Henry Cavill had the dumbest haircut I’ve ever seen.
Very skippable. Matthew Vaughn’s legacy is now as a meh celeb-filled action director. Oh how he’s fallen.
I wonder how many seconds after stepping into that room Bob Dylan regretted the decision to show up. Was it under 5?
Since this was Danny McBride’s entree into Hollywood, I’ll say, nice start! This films had some highlights certainly, but also felt fairly low budget in the production and the writing at times.
Two episodes in and the show’s good but not as great as Band of Brothers (yet), still many hours left to be watched.
Austin Bulter’s down to only 40% Elvis now.
Am I supposed to believe that Ben’s traveling frequently for his job listening to Unwritten on single repeat the whole time?
Fun movie with some pretty bad writing.
I liked this series, but for me it never fully clicked. They did stick a landing, but it really only resolved the Curse portion while not addressing the rest.
The whole series felt like it was less than the sum of its parts. You’d think adding a Safdie and Nathan would create a masterpiece but maybe they canceled each other out a bit.

Certainly not the movie I was expecting from the trailers. That plot line is like the 3rd story in the movie. It’s very well written and dryly, cynically, ironically funny, Monk is a great character and a great Jeffrey Wright performance.
In the end, it did leave me wanting more, despite this being a few separate movies tied into one. I wanted more of the book plot line and more of the father story.
A fine parent trap-y switch movie. I liked the Cameron Diaz coupling more than the Kate Winslet one.
The first one without Wes and you could feel that it was missing some of his magic. Well, I’m now caught up. I watched them in 7, 1-6 order and knew the killer from this one already.
Melissa was a good new lead, and politics aside, I’m sad she won’t be in the newest one (Scream 8?)
This movie manages to be fairly Christian messaged, despite its atheist/god-skeptic framing. I’m probably going to forget that I saw this movie in a week or so.
This definitely feels like a story worth telling, so, thanks Obama.
While I did enjoy learning about Bayard Rustin’s life, this was a bit of a slog, and a lot of boardroom.
Wow this movie was a lot. Most of it was really good, with the writing and the performances being the standout facets.

There were nearly a dozen stories which they landed successfully, a really impressive feat while maintaining a high quality dialogue. The movie felt quite long, and I think the ultimate thesis would’ve been just as strong without one of the stories.
It was a reboot, or so it told me, and it was quite good. It captured enough of a spirit of the original, it brought in some great new blood. It did everything a Scream needs to do.

Did Jesse Eisenberg narrate the first one, because that may’ve been the worst part of a pretty bad movie. Zoey Deutch was uniquely bad for her career, a strong contender in a crowded field of “worst parts”. This movie was so unfunny, it’s hard to explain how bad the jokes were.
Also, did Woody put into his contract that he needed to sing every 20 minutes?

This is one of those movies that you can tell the actors had more fun making than I had watching. If you ended the movie after the opening credits and text, you’d have a more interesting movie than the one I watched

Schlocky garbage which is lacking in any of the fun of the main series. The humor from the overly self-serious leads is awful, and the guest stars are lazy. Vanessa Kirby didn’t realize what movie she was in and turned in a performance entirely too good for this flick.
Imagine DJ Khaled signing you. His notes would start and end with, “scream your own name at the beginning of your song”.
A slightly above average shitty action movie. Beekeeper is just John Wick but with bees instead of dogs, and vagueness instead of the continental. More dumb funny than bad dumb but only just barely.
Also why on earth is Paramount still using the Miramax name?
A deeply Massachusetts vehicle for some standout performances from some great actors.
That was a decent Pete set. It took a bit before I was into it, but he got there.
The man liked women and little cars that go vroom, and in both he had about a 50% crash and burn rate. Some good performances here, a mostly exciting story but it never fully clicked for me.
I guess it’s time to see if Letterboxd has any content moderation.

This film depicts the most evil perpetrators of the Holocaust during all of the hours where they weren’t directly killing Jews. I’m left trying to pin culpability onto the wife and children, living in a Polish Jew’s stolen property, directly adjacent to the death camp of death camps, blissfully ignoring the genocide being constantly orchestrated within earshot.

But where are the Jews?!? The only Jews we see are anonymous masses, represented by nameless and faceless extras, shoes, suitcases, and other discarded items of the dead. Or, house staff confirmed to be Jewish by remarks that “we could have you gassed”.

I spent the whole movie waiting for the Soviets to roll in and smack the grin off all of the Nazis trying to live in their stolen “Lebensraum”, but the film was too cowardly to show that, just like they couldn’t muster up the courage to show a single Jew sent to their death.
I wanted some kind of redemption, wherein these direct beneficiaries of the Holocaust would see the comeuppance, but this wasn’t the film for that either. What we’re left with is a depiction of:
