a blissful, familial, ol’ timey Nazi family tale, were it not for that pesky human burning factory next door, coupled with the story of a man so good at his job of human killing that he keeps getting promoted, drat.And I just didn’t need to see that coming from Germany without really any engagement with the severity of the crimes depicted.
If you think the two greatest musicians to grace this world are The Beatles and Ed Sheeran, this is the film for you. This was such a slog and a bore.

I loved this because I really enjoy Mean Girls the Musical, and I love Mean Girls the movie. So I can overlook the various flaws and enjoy what’s good about this: namely Reneé Rapp (Regina) Auli’i Cravalho (Janis), and Jaquel Spivey (Damian). All of the plastics were good, as was Angourice’s acting, but my three standouts were just on another level.

The musical is written for Regina to shine and Reneé’s singing voice was so refined and powerful and perfect for the part, it was pretty clear she came from the theatre. Really any time that Auli’i or Reneé wasn’t the one singing, I was wishing they were.

I don’t want to be cruel here, but the musical suffered a bit from the rearrangement of songs to compensate for Angourice’s singing. It certainly benefited Auli’i and Jaquel’s singing time, but we lost It Roars, and Cady’s part on Apex Predator. I really wish they’d cast someone with Broadway experience as the lead. It wasn’t fair to have such a novice singer go up against a Disney voice and a Broadway star.
Probably not going to return to the movie, but I’ll definitely be listening to, and rewatching some of the songs.
This is off to an alright start (1 episode in), but I will say that Disney’s TV-MA still strays far more family-friendly than Netflix’s earlier Marvel content.
If you’ve seen Reservation Dogs, you’ll recognize a lot of familiar faces, glad that Native actors are getting good work these days.

reviews.filmTitle: Rebel Moon – Part One: A Child of Fire
paragraphs: I have never seen a film trying so hard to be Star Wars nor have I seen one flopping at it this badly. The epitome of style over substance, oops no style edition.
Terrible robotic dialogue. Extremely generic and tired story. Gratuitous and largely pointless slo-mo. Boring and overly serious characters. Frequent, lengthy, and unnecessary exposition dumps.
I will not be watching part two (don’t hold me to this)
A truly harrowing and horrific story of survival. If it didn’t really happen, you wouldn’t believe it was real.

I will say that Netflix really has come out in favorite of the dub. This movie didn’t indicate it was originally in Spanish and just let you pick whatever Audio Track with no indication of which was the recorded one.

They’re on a mission from Gahd, and they don’t care how many police they need to run away from along the way. I love the world that this movie takes place in, despite not totally loving the movie. The characters are great as well, as is all of the music; I can definitely see how this is a classic.
Very much expected them to sing Soul Man…

Similar to Mank, I found myself struggling to care about the characters (Leonard and any supporting part) or the story - I lay the blame squarely at the director’s feet. And is there a lazier trick than using black and white to represent the past?

Also seeing Sarah Silverman, a real Jew, acting alongside fake-nosed Bradley Cooper is like seeing a Black person in a movie with a black-faced character. (For the record, blackface is so, so, so much worse than a fake nose, but I still don’t appreciate Bradley Jew-ing himself up for the role; I can certainly suspend disbelief enough without the schnoz. Why didn’t he feel the need to make Carey more visibly Chilean, but felt the need to make himself more Jewish?)
Lastly, Carey Mulligan was great, no notes.

reviews.filmTitle: Kevin Hart & Chris Rock: Headliners Only
paragraphs: This is not a comedy special, this is a documentary, which I was not expecting. I appreciated learning the backstories from the comics, but this gave the special something of a Walk Hard vibe, where we never really got to see Dewey Cox on stage. There was maybe only two jokes shown from each earlier show, and really nothing shown from their NYC tours but the backstage portions and the very very end.
Bo Burnham did it better in 1/7th the time.

reviews.filmTitle: Curry & Cyanide: The Jolly Joseph Case
paragraphs: This was a pretty crazy story, but all the facts are still somewhat in dispute as the case is still ongoing. I wish they’d waited another year before making this, so that events could’ve been told more concretely.
That being said, assuming everything they’ve accused Jolly of is true, wow that lady had a knack for killing her close family members.
“Black Magic isn’t magic, it’s DNA”
Truly some of the worst writing of 2023. Terrible Guinness product placement, and a boring story, really not much redemptive here.
Maybe watch this on a plane if you’ve seen everything else they’re showing?

A really sad story of a cursed family told compellingly through Zac Efron’s long stares. The story had to jump around quite a bit to tell the many twists and turns of the plot, I would’ve actually loved another hour or two more had they made this a miniseries instead.

I’m glad this was made pre-Taylor, so there’s no backsplanation about this being because of her. Love that they’re giving an Eagle such a great spotlighting documentary. I loved how much kindness they paid to Philly fans, and our teams. Great doc

Definitely my favorite Trevor Noah special. At his worst l, he relies far too heavily on his accent and stereotype jokes, but here he balanced that so well with his other styles of humor and it just all clicked.
If you’re going to only watch one special of his, I’d recommend this Trever Noah standup hour.

As someone who’s spent a lot of time in America, and a bit of time in China, this film so wonderfully captures both lived experiences. The Farewell manages to be so dryly funny and heartfelt at the same time, while existing entirely within reality.

In short, I loved this movie. This is Awkwafina at her absolute best. And as someone whose Mandarin skills are waning by the day, I could understand 95% of what Awkwafina was saying, she’s uniquely understable.
The movie is 70% in Mandarin.

A tale of morality and the complexity around doing what’s right when the bigotry of society forces you to live your life a lie. Wonderful writing enables this amount of introspection in such a short amount of time.
Slow and dry and too dark. Should’ve been called First Biscuit.

reviews.filmTitle: Under Pressure: The U.S. Women's World Cup Team
paragraphs: The framing of the series is interesting, because everyone is trying to explain away a known, negative end result. Definitely not the documentary the filmmakers were initially expecting to make.
A really tender, sweet, onion of a story. If you asked me to guess in act one to predict what happens in act three, I wouldn't get anything right.

The strangest thing about the movie is the pivot. It starts out as this mother and son story, which you think is going to go predictably one way, which would’ve been fine. Then it flips everything and tells a much better story. Had they not done the flip and just established the latter story from the beginning, the film may’ve been improved (that may be a hot take).
The Cruellafication of Willy.

Let me start with the positives:
- Hugh Grant was more charming than ever, somehow.
- Loved the class narratives framing the greedy against the needy.

Now the negatives:
- Matt Lucas and his Hitler mustache and haircut.
- Olivia Colman, with a rare miss. The character just didn’t work for me.
- The magic. It never felt whimsical, and Willy never felt magical at all.
- The fact that Wonka’s first strategy for distracting guards is to drug them….
This had some really fun action set pieces, mixed with some close up shots that I hated.

So deeply moving and impactful, you watch a lifetime pass through the eyes of a largely neglected and abused Black woman in the early 20th century. It’s brutal to watch at times, but satisfying at the resolve, really Spielberg operating at the height of his prowess.
I’m really not excited to see a glitzy remake of this, even with Spielberg’s production.
Whoopie was great, as was Oprah. Danny Glover was terrifying. Also Larry Fishburne in the credit made me guffaw.

Really disappointed to get this from Esmail, and…. the Obamas? Ok, sure. The story was really predictable, and not at all satisfying. Albeit it’s hard to be late on any trend, much less one as tired as the end of world disaster movie.

I really felt like they wasted Julia Roberts and didn’t give her anything to work with more than a B horror movie. I assume she was a big Mr. Robot fan too, and signed on to work with Sam, or maybe to work with Barack, or Mahershala, who knows.
I too have explorer in my blood.

What a delight was this. Adding to my enjoyment was the extremely squeamish person I was sat next to. He flinched and recoiled for all of the medical and sexual scenes, which make up about 30% of the runtime.
Never been more convinced that birds aren’t real.
Miyazaki came back to make his Pan’s Labyrinth with sprinkles of Interstellar
This had a few good laughs and some Harold And Kumar energy at times.
Gotta support Lili’s post-Riverdale career

What an interesting and meta take on the popularization of criminal behavior. I think it’s especially interesting coming from Natalie Portman, who was herself sexualized from a similar age to the character in the story.
I think it’s my favorite Natalie Portman role since Black Swan.

The fact that Pat Boone existed is so shameful on this country.
I’m glad that Little Richard got a modicum of the respect that
he deserved at the end of his life.

An emotional exploration of the value of life, loss, and trauma which just so happens to have a Godzilla in it. I don’t think a kaiju movie to date has so successfully nailed the human portions of the story.
Maybe the whole Zach and Florence relationship wasn’t a mistake.

Really touching and personal look into Jon and his wife, Suleika’s, personal lives and she battles cancer and he… is extremely successful and sad (can’t really describe it well). It’s worth watching and has some pretty fun music.

This one’s probably on me, but as someone who didn’t know who John le Carré, David Cornwell, or Errol Morris was going in, I was a bit confused at times. Cool story, but I missed many of the literary/film references.
What a fun flick this was! This was really made at the perfect time, when the animation looked just passable enough to still be watchable 25 years later.
I miss fun Will Smith and end credit raps!
Jake LaMotto’s got a real problem with jealousy.
The prototypical fucked up boxer movie. It was good, but it’s been so copied that it’s hard to reflect on how special this must’ve felt in 1980.
The grandpa goes pretty quickly from saying, “stay away from my grandchild” to “sure fly off to that remote island with him”

I’m an avowed gangster movie disliker, but Scarface certainly transcends the genre. It’s an incredible rags to riches to ashes story, bolstered by Al Pacino’s great portrayal of the very flawed Tony Montana.

This movie was over-and-above-all strange. It had a strange mismatch of tones showing sadism as comedic as times, as the whole airport staff picks on the protagonist, who was played as sympathetic just a scene prior. The Zoe Saldana : Diego Luna long-distance, cross-terminal romance was strange. At least it certainly depicted post-9/11 flying as the hellscape that the TSA made it.

Wish, The Lion King, and The Hunchback of Notre Dame are the only Disney movies which advocate for regicide, and Lion King is more of a family drama than a kingly one. This movie and Hunchback each get credit for suggesting offing the ruling authority when the populace faces unjust adversity. Unfortunately, this movie doesn’t even know its own lesson, and ends the movie by saying “keep wishing!”.
Apart from the shown-not-stated lesson of this film, and an okay song or two, there really wasn’t much there.
A touching story of a young immigrant family’s pursuit of the American dream as they move to the countryside to start a farm. Both adult leads shine in their respective roles.
The film is more than 80% in Korean.

As someone that doesn’t love gangster movies, this was fine. The de-aging didn’t fully work for me, to ebbed and flowed.
Also the length was a lot. It felt merited for the story, but the film carries a heavy footprint regardless.
A fun, fantastical story with a great performance from the always excellent Nic Cage. The story was at its weakest when it was tackling cancel culture, which is an admittedly tough topic to tackle.

reviews.filmTitle: The Killing of a Sacred Deer
paragraphs: Weird and horrific, but in a good, artsy kinda way.

reviews.filmTitle: Mike Birbiglia: The Old Man and the Pool
paragraphs: Deeply personal. I wanted this to be funnier, but I get why you’d want to balance the tone.
Legitimately one of the funniest movies of the year, with such an iconic ending.
Oliver Quick likes to get shirtless and he likes to get freaky, and we get to watch him do both of them, a lot. Definitely go see this movie, if only for Rosamund Pike, who’s spectacular.

Ridley Scott’s Napoleon is a hollow incomplete man with some deep insecurities. In a strangely edited movie, Joaquin Phoenix wasn’t given the most runway and came off Michael Scott-y at times. This movie was somehow both overly long, and not nearly long enough.
Charming bear flick

So seldom does a remake feel “worth it”, but this one certainly elevates the original. They reimagined the whole story, and while being meta about the source material tells a new story. It’s great that they got the entire original cast back as well.
The sweetest Sandler movie and by far the most musical
Beautiful editing and direction, with some great music and an appreciably out-there story.

reviews.filmTitle: A Murder at the End of the World
paragraphs: Not the show that I was expecting from the description. Emma Corrin is great, the rest of the show still needs to win me over.

reviews.filmTitle: The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes
paragraphs: Movie was too damn long, but there was a surprising amount that I liked about this prequel; you could carve this into a pretty nice 2 hour movie.

Jason Schwartzman was incredible, no notes. Viola Davis was likewise excellent. Rachel Ziegler gave her best Woodie Guthrie - I definitely think she’s best in roles that let her sing. I have to say that Tom Blyth turned in a performance I could best describe as Justin Timberlaking it.

reviews.filmTitle: How to Become a Mob Boss
paragraphs: There is definitely some law of diminishing returns going on with these, each is worse than its predecessor. And yet my dumb ass keeps watching these and telling Netflix to make more of them.
This one just tells you to kill people in every episode.
High anxiety the whole time. That’s the Safdie Guarantee.

It’s one joke and it gets old, fast. This movie would be funny if it had Three Stooges levels of physical comedy, but instead it’s an inside Hollywood movie mocking LA people, with a cast filled with A-listers and Sunny cast members.

It felt dark and moody and Fincher-y. As I’ve never really loved the “man who kills for a living” genre, the slight dislike here may be personally and broadly mine. But I wanna see this without any voiceover dialogue, I think that may’ve been more interesting.
Bad movie, terrible premise

As someone that’s been a Robbie Williams fan since they he existed in 2014, it was great to see all of these historical bits that I didn’t quite understand, and get the real context behind Angels and Let Me Entertain You. And from there it was a but bumpier, but I liked learning about all of Robbie’s tribulations, and his long road to where he is today.

Wonderfully hearted film about two mirrored twins: half their problems they share, the other half they have the opposite problems. My highlights were the writing and the perfect depiction of both border school antics (they got shiiking picture perfect).

The writing was so phenomenal and the technical standout of the picture.  It was funny, heartwarming, and deeply emotionally affective, weaving in both a class narrative and a personal picture about an unfortunate trio (all of whom were excellent).

The other bit that they got perfect was celebrating holidays with strange groups of people. As someone that’s been on their own for more than half their life now, I’ve ended up with some strange groupings over the holidays, and this captured so many of my lived experiences.
This movie showed a remarkably wide swath of the various portions of my life, down to mentioning Swarthmore (my childhood home).
Fun fact, Ms. Marvel, everything that’s ever existed has traveled through both time and space to get right here to this very moment.
This was perfectly fine.

Admittedly, I had never really put much thought into Elvis’ early years with Priscilla, and how much of a literal child groomer he was. Now, I can’t get much further in this review without noting how way too tall Jacob Elordi was to play Elvis. 5” too tall, which made him look so goofy, even with Sofia Coppola trying her best.

This entire movie was carried by Cailee Spaeny’s performance, elevated by Coppola’s direction. She plays a 14 year old so effectively that I mentally yelled, “don’t give drugs to that child, Elvis” multiple times. Very excited to see what Cailee does next, and I remain a Coppola fan.
The movie was perfectly fine, but Will Ferrell gave such a good tribute to Alex Trebeck, who was by all accounts incredibly kind, while still being a smart ass / asshole at times.
Wolf of Wall Street but drugs and no fun or funny.
Chris Evans really needs to shake things up and do a simple rom-com or something self-aware or cheesy. Since Knives Out all of his projects have been so flat.

reviews.filmTitle: Big Vape: The Rise and Fall of Juul
paragraphs: This documentary doesn’t know how it feels about vaping. It was good, but it was very balanced between the pro and anti vaping camps.
The one constant is the painting of Big Tobacco as the bad guy, which is some low hanging fruit, but ultimately comes across as the Spider-man pointing meme.

We love a spiteful revenge documentary. Oh man, they used It’s Always Sunny music, and I immediately started laughing. But it gets so, so touching by the end. You’ll leave loving the man, and being angry at the bear.

Marty’s Schindler’s List, so far as this seems to be an extremely personal story to him set during a time of orchestrated mass death of a minority people. A deeply affecting film which is carried by the excellent performances up and down the call sheet.

Normally, I balk at anything longer than 2.5 hours (I still haven’t seen the Irishman 😬 I’ll probably watch it shortly), but this movie really respects your time. I wouldn’t cut any more than 10 minutes of the finished product.

My biggest downside was the ancient couple sitting next to me: both whisper-yelling throughout the movie. The man, in some need to feel smart, made frequent obvious remarks - literally screaming “oil” the first time a black puddle was shown on screen, as if he’d struck it himself. In total providing a real-time 4th grade film analysis of the movie (he literally said “look, it’s the good guys” when the FBI finally arrive). The women couldn’t follow anything, crying “why did they do that?” after the narrative spends ten minutes setting up a murder both visually and in the text.

We live in an age of great documentaries / docuseries, but folks, this wasn’t it. The story was fine, but it really felt like the story of the Rocky statue at the Philly Art Museum, which Sly bought himself and the museum reluctantly decided not to throw it out (they moved it out of the way pretty quickly). This doc felt like it was more for Sly than for an external audience.

There’s a kernel of a lesson to the story which is to keep trying and to do it yourself if no one else will give it to you. I think Rob McElhenney (sp?) and the It’s Always Sunny guys have the better version of that story.

reviews.filmTitle: Now and Then - The Last Beatles Song
paragraphs: As much a testament to the technology which recovered John’s voice as it is to the band. It’s a bit of a shame that Paul spends the whole time defending the making of the song, but I’m happy to accept that this is the final Beatles “thing” (song + special) that we’re likely to get from all 4 of the boys.

Well, the action is far more intelligible than the earlier Bay ones. Unfortunately that’s only one of the myriad of shortcomings of the Transformers film series. They always opt to add a bunch of strange and unnecessary plot details (like why does the kid have sickle cell anemia?) which don’t serve the plot and aren’t used in the text enough to justify their inclusion.

Also common among the Transformers movies, this one had far too much human stuff, and not nearly enough robo-stuff. Anthony Ramos is great, but entirely superfluous in a movie about a team up between Transformers and Robo-Apes. They always introduce some McGuffin to keep the humans relevant through the latter acts, and it’s beyond old after half a dozen of these movies. It’s like they want to stick an Indiana Jones movie into the Robo movie (and no, being meta about it doesn’t help at all). Just give me a solid Robo movie before you try to give us all of this.
Also x2, it’s so weird to me that Transformers can turn into anything, but can’t get rid of their little logos; it’s like the Pokémon Ditto being unable to get the eyes right.

At one level, it feels like it’s going for something Dr. House-y, but the writing is so poor that it really never hits those levels. The story is likewise pretty flat and unimpressive. The sum of its parts is just kind of disappointing medical gore flick.

reviews.filmTitle: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
paragraphs: This was adorable! Lord and Miller before they’d got their full act together, but still firing on all cylinders.
Visually, nothing was wet, and I kinda wanted to see some wet at some point. Oh and I loved the Brentdeption arc.
Elizabeth Zott is the new Lydia Tarr
Many thoughts!

- First, and most obviously, thank you for excluding everything that has been shown in a live action remake.
- Second, and most importantly, where was my main man Max Goof?!? There’s no way that they didn’t invite Goofy’s son to the party.

The movie that kicked off the final wave of parody movies. I grew up on Superhero Movie and other garbage movies which came after. While this really hasn’t aged well, it was still pretty funny and felt like a real movie.

Didn’t realize that Weinstein’s Miramax made both this and Scream. The worst man found a great way to double-dip on the same content, his movie career would be aspirational if he wasn’t so personally (and behind-the-scenes professionally) evil.
This film decided to subject itself to the trilogy curse, and certainly wasn’t as good as the first two.

Oh, the gall of Harvey Weinstein’s Miramax to produce this movie with a plot line about a sexually abusive movie predator ruining everyone’s lives. I guess that exemplifies the power of that horrible man in Hollywood.

A really interesting exploration on subjectivity and voracity as you witness a death and its subsequent trial unfold. You’re given morsel-by-morsel of information, which slowly paints a picture of the marriage.
While you don’t need to see this in theatres, you’ll need to see this one eventually as it’s bound to be a frontrunner come Oscar-time.
40% of this movie was in English, with the other 60% being in French.
What an incredible movie, that I’d only ever seen bits and chunks of. Probably the best horror movie that I’ve seen, but that’s Kubrick for ya.
I was just on the Santa Cruz boardwalk last week! It was a lot less life changing for me, anyways.
I finally watched the sparkly vampire movie! I was pretty surprised by the lack of werewolves and that Edward was way more glittery than sparkly.
This was quite a movie.
Really cool to set a horror film in the world of dreams, I really enjoyed the introduction of Freddy Krueger. Looks like Wes Craven’s always had it.
This was fun but had way too many “weren’t the 80s so wacky?” and “but that didn’t exist in the 80s” moments.

reviews.filmTitle: The Ringleader: The Case of the Bling Ring
paragraphs: This subject matter was far too minor for even a 90minute documentary. Honestly, they should stop giving publicity to these kids, even if for the sake of trying to rectify the original situation.
Not nearly as good as the first, but still pretty fun. After seeing three of these movies, I can confidently say that I’m a fan of this series!
Beware the creepy, drunk, racist, rural Aussie.
I wanted this to be so much better, but the product was fairly half-baked, with lots of poor decisions for the sake of plot advancing.
The horror movie where every character wants me to know that they’ve seen more horror movies than me.

We’re in the golden age of sports docuseries, with this, Jordan’s one, Magic’s two, Tiger’s one; the list goes on. As with all the best ones, I left this series loving the subject so much more. I love David and all his tidiness eccentricities, and I’ve always been a Posh spice fan. Posh and Becks are the best power couple, and I don’t really mind them dodging the whole cheating scandal.

A 90minute, original, A24, comedy musical - what’s not to love? Legitimately funny, and a decent musical, I’m absolutely seeing whatever these gays do next. I hope it’s Jeffrey What Have You Done: A Musical
A loving ode to one of the masters of cinema, told pretty heavily in his own voice. This would make an interesting double feature with The Fabelmans.
As a quick warning, this will show the biggest moments and endings of basically all of Spielberg’s films. It spoiled a few for me, which I didn’t love.
There’s one thing you can guarantee about a John Carney film, music will be an integral part of the story, and this film stays true to the pattern. And who wouldn’t fall for JGL’s dreamy strumming?

Excellent style, fine substance

My theatre was mostly empty, and this movie deserves to be seen in theatres. Go see it!
Kids these days just don’t bully like they used to

reviews.filmTitle: The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar
paragraphs: Leave it to Wes Anderson to invent the visual audiobook. The real set pieces gave Blues Clues in the best way.
The second I heard a folksy narrator waxing poetically about the past I said, “did Stephen King write this”?
Also that middle aged man looked nothing like Wil Wheaton.

Why were the Persian warriors 8-10’ tall orcs and wizards? There are definitely some European/Asian racial overtones going on here. This would’ve been less uncomfortable if these weren’t the ancestors of living people today.
And for a fun and lethal drinking game: take a shot every time Gerard Butler sounds Scottish.
Gael García Bernal gives an incredible performance that shines in a largely fine film. The best scenes are the dramatic ones, as the film is carried by the performance.
The wrestling was comprehendible, which is always appreciated for physical performances.
The film is nearly entirely bilingual in Spanish and English.
I would own a super pig, and I would eat a super pig. It’s really a “yes, and” situation for me.

paragraphs: I was doubtful of the movie’s title until she smelled that one guy
Jimmy Tatro will be playing high schoolers when he’s in his 60s.

I think this movie made me realize that I hate comedies where people are playing themselves surrounded by actors playing characters. So it gets credit for that, and probably nothing else. Mark Hamill, why did you take this role?
Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter meets The Death of Stalin. It works far more than it doesn’t, though it did get truly absurd at times.
Nearly the whole film was in English.
A really sweet story of a guy who just wanted to have fun. Of course they’d cast Charlie Day to portray him, in some extremely unnecessary reenactments.

Wow, this film relied so heavily on green screens and really bad CGI. Expend-4-bles is not a movie to be paused; I can only imagine how bad those pan shots look frozen, when the effects looked that bad at full speed. The first scene Megan Fox was in with any other actors was the final one of the movie. Also 50 Cent is in a scene, playing a military assassin, and PIMP is playing on a speaker that other characters react to.

The writing was atrocious, it felt like it was written by a high schooler. The first half hour was characters just stating exposition at one another. It ended up being accidentally funny once or twice, but definitely not enough to compensate for the jokes that fell flat.

I’m sorry but we do need to talk about Dolph’s storyline. He starts out 6 months sober, which has made him a terrible shot. In the climax of the film, he starts drinking again and magically regains his shooting ability. What lesson am I supposed to take away from this? Sobriety makes you worse at your job? Alcohol and guns is a good combo?
Quentin Unchained
Wow, I loved this so much, instant classic. This entire thing lives or dies on Jennifer Garner’s performance, and she’s incredible, and you can’t help but fall in love with Mark Ruffalo.

Cheating’s not cool, even if your boyfriend is an especially asshole-y Alec Baldwin character. It is so unclear to me what Anna sees in William other than him looking like peak-attractiveness Hugh Grant.

Every scene felt like it was stretched 30% longer than it needed to be to compensate for the super short story. Loved the “fuck the rich” story and Paul Dano’s incredibly endearing character, but didn’t love the movie.
“This is about race wars”, Brian talking about cars.
Watching this movie, you’d have no idea that Tyrese will one day go to space and become invincible.
Right on the edge of being funny. If I rewatch this in a few years, my score’s going to be lower.
I still see purple people too
Excellent performances by Jolie and Ryder, and a pretty decent mid-century asylum film. It scratches the itch that Shutter Island, Shawshank, and One Flew all scratch.
It was good but it was no Sharkboy and Lavagirl
I hated how this movie was shot. Was the script 10 pages long? If you take out all of the drug montages, this movie would be 30 minutes long.

It turns out, before dog, dino was man’s best friend. It takes a lot of guts to set your series before the invention of language, where you’re locked in to visual storytelling. In the instance of Primal, it gives room for the animation to shine.
Also I do wish David Attenborough would narrate an episode of this series for April Fools.
Ok, this movie lived up to the very high expectations its rating set. The Handmaiden may be tied with The Lives of Others for the most shots of someone peeping through a hole.

reviews.filmTitle: You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah
paragraphs: Probably the best possible outcome for an Adam Sandler bat mitzvah movie. This was a charming movie that made me feel super old.

reviews.filmTitle: Scouts Honor: The Secret Files of the Boy Scouts of America
paragraphs: The Boy Scouts didn’t check government IDs for scout masters?!?! And no state government, nor the federal government has looked into any of the allegations?!? I worked at numerous summer camps growing up, and had to give so much info and submit formal background checks. This doc made it so clear how willfully blind the whole organization was to this problem, and how our elected officials have failed to act on this network of abuse. Simply disgraceful.
As a bit of an aside, my cat came with the name “Scout” and I charged it because my only association with the word was this pedophilic organization.
Such a powerful film. As a Quaker, I love a film with a non-violent message. Outstanding film by a young director and pre-all star cast.
Laurence Fishburne gave an incredible performance; I wish Furious was my dad. Really impressed with Ice Cube too, he could act (albeit the role was not a huge stretch).
Also with Dooky sucking on a pacifier the whole film, Ricky walking around drinking a quart of milk, the 90s were an insane time.
This was definitely my fault, but I hyped up “the Eminem movie” over the last 15 years. This was a perfectly meh biopic, which my brain registered as a boxing parody movie, for some reason.
It all builds to the end where you’re asking yourself, “will Eminem open his mouth and be Eminem, or will he not say anything?” Not great stakes lol

Ep 1: This is a me problem, but I just don’t find football interesting enough to enjoy this. Tim Tebow was fine but this didn’t have the raucousness of Jonny Manziel to keep me tuned in. 4 episodes is a lot, I’m probably out
I always knew this as the movie with the youngest Jonas and the youngest Cyrus, but wow the English dub has an A list cast. Liam Neesom’s Fujimoto was especially good.

Miyazaki’s Little Mermaid is maybe his most child-friendly and child-aged movie (either this or Totoro). While I certainly didn’t love it, Ponyo was a really charming movie which had its shining moments; I definitely liked it.
Timothée gives a captivating performance as a spiraling drug addict, and you can’t help but feel for, clearly excellent father, Steve Carell trying his hardest to father him back to health.

One note as a local, when Nic goes to sulk at the Golden Gate bridge lookout, he’s going to be paying $8 to get back home. Not the best investment for a drug addict. Sulk atop of Twin Peaks, or Corona Heights, or hell San Bruno summit.
Woman finds her place in a capitalist society
Miyazaki loves flying so much. It’s evident from this film alone, but so much clearer across his career.

reviews.filmTitle: The Lego Movie 2: The Second Part
paragraphs: Huge step down from the first one
This was a lot campier than I expected, and way more fun.
An absolute time capsule of the mid 2000s zeitgeist, including gaslighting people into believing that thin celebrities were fat.
I love how this and The Dark Knight Rises ended in essentially the same way.
What a beautiful Burton Frankenstein story. I think Johnny Depp’s best weird characters are the quieter ones, he’s so endearing playing the quiet freak in the corner.
Really heartfelt movie
Wachowskis do Spy Kids with a healthy sprinkle of LazyTown.

While I didn’t love the face design and movements, the musical underscoring certainly made up for it. The music carried the movie from scene to scene. Also the old Clubhouse was an incredible invention, something so magical that could only come from a Miyazaki.

reviews.filmTitle: John Mulaney & The Sack Lunch Bunch
paragraphs: I didn’t hate this as much as I was expecting to! Oh John, the irony of opening this saying, “I’ll never have children”.

Definitely the weakest of the specials, and not just because it’s 40% wife guy stuff - which has not aged well. But I still love John and it’s still hilarious and better than most other comedy specials out there.
One of my favorite comedy specials of all time. I quote these bits all the time. It’s incredible to see how far John has come since 2012, when he joked about not being able to fill the auditorium.
And I thought Birds of Prey had a stupidly long title.
Did you know Sony still makes a walkman? Now you do
Noah Baumback can so accurately capture the internal friction of Jewish family life, it’s almost uncomfortable.
A beautiful but bittersweet story of Black love and life in America.
The 2020 sketches were much better
Needs more Ayo
I would eat Rachel’s beefcakes (if baked medium).
Ayo and Rachel are the new Abbi and Ilana
Here for whatever Ayo and/or Rachel wants to do
Nonstop, continuous action and violence as a few man defeat an army.

A pretty damning, all-encompassing documentary on the fault of the 2008 mortgage crisis, they break it all down for you nicely. You can see how this level of outrage would spur an Occupy Wall Street movement.
Also Matt Damon’s along for the ride providing narration, which post “fortune favors the brave” crypto scam, feels a bit cheapened.
I’m glad this documentary has the framing that it does as it’s shining a light on an enormous fame-chaser fraudster. I assume Kanye’s basketball academy had a similarly disastrous experience.
So it turns out PJ was fingering herself the whole time

So many thoughts. I really loved Baylan and Shin, the new sith. Having no experience with either character, Sabine and Ezra both really grew on me to be likable characters. I definitely didn’t need that much of the Skywalkers (plural) in this show.
All in all, a decent show. Happy that I watched it, obviously need to watch the follow up (which is now just “every other Star Wars show” I guess - ugh). It was fine.
Well at least now I’ll have an answer if anyone ever asks what my least favorite Fincher film is.

New York was the main character in this movie in a way I’ve never seen before. There’s a flash dance in Times Square to New York, New York to convince JT to move to NYC. A character points out that a fake movie scene wasn’t really shot in NY. Was this movie sponsored by the NYC bureau of tourism?
Also, I love how canonically stupid they made JT’s character.
Oh the disappointment I got from Googling if Seaworld still has whales in 2023. Free the goddamn whales, how is this still a thing?
And when the world is run by horses, then we’ll truly be in a patriarchy.
Also rip Anton Yelchin, an absolute legend and incredible talent.

Edward Snowden is a hero and a patriot. While the execution of this documentary was a bit odd at times (so much was filmed digital text, or Snowden in a hotel room), it’s content was so powerful to keep the doc compelling.

reviews.filmTitle: Ben Platt: Live from Radio City Music Hall
paragraphs: Ben’s got an incredible singing voice, but those literal hand gestures kill me.

reviews.filmTitle: John Mulaney: Kid Gorgeous at Radio City
paragraphs: Truly John Mulaney at his best. While a product of its time, this gave so many icon bits from the horse in the hospital to street smarts.
Never has running felt more like human-horse racing than when a shady non-doctor is monitoring your urine
This was a surprisingly fun movie. Shoutout George Lopez, Low Rider played in my head like half a dozen times. This brought in aspects of Venom, Iron Man, Batman, and Watchman - at least visually.
A story of equal parts tragedy and horror as five men are wrongly convicted of a brutal assault and rape through a mixture of racism and police incompetence.
Ep 1: It’s crazy how blatant this fraud was. I’m definitely hooked into this story.
Ep 2: The story keeps getting crazier and crazier. I’m betting the police came up with the whole thing at this point.
Also, I really hope Pat isn’t dead
Ep 3: Patrick, I love you buddy, but you can’t interview politicians.

A beautiful mosaic film comprised of predominantly hand-drawn styled animation, with some live action documentary footage stitched in. It’s truly a harrowing story of what people have to go through to emigrate to a new country as a refugee.
Hired her because he liked the way she ate lunch, okay then. This was a weird slice of life movie with an overly perfect protagonist. It gave Linklater vibes, in a way.

It’s interesting watching this with the perspective that four years of history brings, where Lula is now president again. It’s scary how quickly a few people can override the votes and will of millions, but at the same time inspiring, that it can reverse itself within two election cycles.
The bloodiest kids you know

paragraphs: An epic end to an excellent trilogy (or I guess the series is continuing?). I hope we can all agree that Steve Zahn ape was the Jar Jar Binks of this franchise.
Fuck the NCAA, I’m glad Johnny got paid, A&M built a stadium on his name.

reviews.filmTitle: Robin Williams: Come Inside My Mind
paragraphs: Touching tribute to the legendary comedian, actor and performer. It really felt like this showed a full picture of the man, with his more quiet private life behind the public persona and various tribulations.

reviews.filmTitle: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
paragraphs: The humans are holed up in my office lobby - the building one block past the Federal Reserve building in SF. They got the shot down market street somewhat wrong, but this was still really cool.

reviews.filmTitle: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
paragraphs: The apes are headed to Napa, they’re going to wine country!Caesar’s a pretty great leader. I’m not even rooting for the humans at this point.
New life goal: return in spirit form at my murder trial and lie to make myself look better.
Tom Hanks has really nailed the “I’m a child in an adult’s body” acting, which makes it super uncomfortable when a woman starts dating him. 80’s scripts were something else.
Charlie Hunnam and Robert Pattinson should’ve swapped parts. Charlie Hunnam didn’t have the rizz to carry this long and fairly unsatisfying movie.
Making an animated climbing movie is such a brilliant idea (as was making a graphic novel about climbing). When done well, you can capture all of the action, anticipation, and horror so vividly.
This movie made me both never want to climb alone, and never want to climb with a lead climber; that’s a real accomplishment.
Uncomfortably relatable movie

reviews.filmTitle: How to Become a Cult Leader
paragraphs: Thanks, Netflix. Your previous series has helped me overthrow a few country’s democratically elected governments. I’m now excited to focus my efforts on amassing a large cult following.

paragraphs: This was directed by half of The Mitchells Vs. The Machines team and had about half the visual pizzazz. That being said, this was still a wonderfully charming kids film.
The humans were uglier than the mutants, and that’s probably the point.
Damn if this isn’t one beautiful looking film. It’s got a weird what if West Side Story was adapted back into a straight play thing going on, which is fine. Also Ponyboy is such a ridiculous name.
They just like, forgot to animate most of the meg’s waves.

reviews.filmTitle: Glitch: The Rise & Fall of HQ Trivia
paragraphs: Pretty boring doc that was way longer than it needed to be.
Side note: when HQ was a thing, everyone said I looked like Scott, and I can see it.
Movie really explained ghosts with a venn diagram

This was way funnier than I was expecting it to be - near constant jokes with a decent hit rate. It’s my first Christopher Guest movie and this has made me way more excited to continue going through his filmography.
Definitely one of the better Pete Davidson and Machine Gun Kelly movies; they work best as canonical fuckups and disappointments.
Love seeing Edward 40hands being represented in film, this was my culture in college. Also a great Raymour & Flanigan shout out, what more could a movie need.
This film made me think about the sheer horror and anxiety of being Ben Platt’s stage manager, I can’t even imagine how bad that job would be.
Anyways, this thing felt super half-baked. Some of the jokes hit, but overall this was a somewhat disappointing watch.
Short and sweet little doc to the Webb telescope and the trials and tribulations it took to build it.
It’s weird to establish that the audience is all straight men and then start a ton of your jokes with “ladies…”
Howard Ashman was brilliant, one-of-a-kind talent, who produced such a prodigious body of work and left too soon.
Attack of the Clones
The Mattel CEO is an escaped Allen
Wow, Val sucks. She’s a terrible friend, I’d happily be the normal sidekick to a superhero; that’s badass.
This was a good, tragic origin story for Atom Eve, and definitely makes me like her a lot more.
The opening to Steph‘s younger years had some big Dewey Cox energy; Steph Curry needs to think about his whole life before he goes on the court.
The pacing for this biopic was a bit off as it felt very slow then quite rushed. But I get why they structured the duel storylines how they did.

Armando Iannucci is so good at capturing the awkward humor that exists in politics. Buschemi and Jason Isaacs were definitely the standouts, but the whole ensemble cast really shined, and elevated the writing.
I’m definitely going to use the line, “I’m more sweat than man” in the future.

If there’s one thing that Nolan knows how to do, it’s to give a good climax, and gee willikers does he deliver. It felt like the climax of this 3hour behemoth goes on for nearly 45minutes, in the best way possible.
Where this movie falls flattest is in the interpersonal, emotional beats. Nolan really gets the intrapersonal drama, but even when delivering among his better work, still hasn’t mastered that.
Also, while this movie definitely had the most understandable dialogue of Nolan’s last decade of films, he still could have mixed the sound better at times.
Now that he’s made one of the better biopics, I’d love to see him challenge himself with a rom-com.

“You should quit traumatizing women with sexual intercourse. I should know, I’m a medical doctor.”Weird collection of nonstop vignettes. Light in plot (even for Linklater), heavy in conspiracy theories. This contrasts nicely with Wes Anderson’s debut Bottle Rocket, as Wes really hadn’t found his niche, while Richard certainly did.

I figured now was as good of a time as any to watch Jonah’s movie. This was a fine corrupting of a boy story. I guess Jonah was supposed to be Fourth Grade, but it really feels like he wanted to be all of the kids.

As someone who grew up watching Walk Hard, it’s weird to say but, I feel like I knew Johnny Cash’s story well… unfortunately it was all comedy coded. So I couldn’t help but chuckle when his dad said that iconic line.
Great Reese performance of a tragic woman who loved terrible men, and spending years washing off an old cranky one before he magically turned decent.

reviews.filmTitle: STILL: A Michael J. Fox Movie
paragraphs: Michael J. Fox’s positivity makes his fight against Parkinson’s Disease so inspirational. I really enjoyed hearing his life story through his own words.
Joaquin Phoenix’s whole career begs the question, “is this man crazy or a really good actor?” This film more so than most.

While this has a twinge of the Borat magic, it never fully connects. I just dont find the subject matter of Joaquin’s career change to be that compelling for a narrative, especially when it’s so clearly fake. Also this movie was one more reminder of how much I miss Letterman’s talkshow.
First, I love the cute Bat Heels. Second, who put “Gotham” on the statue of liberty? Was it not made by the French in this universe?

This was such a 90s movie from the opening using Powerpoint animations, to the matrix coding on Bruce Wayne’s face on the tunnel, and of course the helmet / tv animations. But this film has everything: bad writing, laundry-sorting gymnastics, trapeze death, Jim Carrey at his wackiest annoying the hell out of Tommy Lee Jones.
Selina Kyle being eaten by cats in that alley should’ve turned her into Charlie Kelly, not Catwoman. She should be down in the sewers playing Night Crawlers with Penguin.
Well, this is definitely the most “normal” Batman and Joker film portrayals I’ve seen.

Keaton’s Batman is weirdly refreshing, when starting with a Nolan Batman (as I have), as he’s not doing the gruff voice and isn’t (on the edge of) killing people. Keaton’s Bruce Wayne is just an absolute weirdo. I don’t know what he’s doing, but it’s strangely charming.

Nicholson’s Joker is just a gangster, and after being dropped in acid, he remained mainly normal; I found him more tame than anything else. I feel like he’s still got a bit too much Cesar Romaro Joker in him. I do think Nicholson gave it his best, and every actor who succeeded him (Hamill, Ledger, and to a much lesser extent, Leto) had a goofier, or more playful, side, which elevated the role.
Oh, and I loved the original Batmobile, super sleek and great gadgets. All-in-all, great job Burton and cast, and a great foundational cinematic Batman.

A one-of-a-kind documentary, as I don’t think many actors with careers as long and prolific as Val Kilmer’s have recorded their whole lives on video. I’ve seen a shockingly few number of his films, but I learned a lot more about the man and respect him quite a bit.
It’s a shame that Val got cancer, it cut an incredible acting talent far too short.
I had never heard of Dolemite, so this was such a fun surprise, and I’ll definitely need to watch the actual film now.
After watching years of Key and Peele on youtube my brain thinks every movie Keegan in is a sketch. He could be playing a Nazi doctor and I’d think to myself, ah what a goofy skit this is.
What if there was one Justin Timberlake, and one Kevin Jonas in a boy band?
Fun villain though I’m so tired of this whole fake face thing.
Definitely the weakest of the Cornetto trilogy, but damn was this a fun time. I could’ve been a smidge shorter, but Edgar Wright really stuck the landing.
Love Edgar Wright’s direction in this one. It’s incredible how much he’s developed his style already this early in his career. I’d only seen Hot Fuzz of the Cornetto Trilogy up until this point.
I appreciated how long you spend in the pre-zombie times, watching as the world falls apart.
Stephanie Hsu killed it, as the standout in a strong foursome. I’d watch a sequel to this. It had some of the funniest lines I’ve seen in a comedy this year.

It seems like Jr. got a lot out of making this doc, and that’s really nice and I’m happy for him. The end product was weird, and fun, and unique, editing in footage from each person’s cut of the film, and from Sr.’s various films.
I’m glad that I got to learn about Sr., both the person and the filmography. He seemed like a fun guy to get into some mischief with. Though probably not the best father, all things considered.
Wow this was a painful watch, I truly don’t know how/why I finished it. I don’t find Kyle Mooney’s weird infantilization funny at all. Also, I kept pausing the movie to watch episodes of The Bear.
Don’t fuck with gay Kiwis.
This was some next level investigative journalism. We need more of this in this world.
Never dug Dug
This film really nailed environmental racism, in all senses of the term
We love some good vasectomy stories

Hwang Woo-suk is such an interesting character because he’s got fairly strong morals, they’re just a few statistical deviations outside of the norm. And he’s been set loose in the U.A.E., which seems very pro-cloning.
Also that one man was waaaaay too obsessed with his dog. He’s got so many statues of this dog, and he held onto the corpse in his fridge, even after taking genetic samples.
A great final watch of Pride month 🌈. A gay knight and a trans(-species) child team up to clear his name. You also get a Try Guy in an epic gay feud, and some Arcane-lite animation.

It has a number of fairly surface-level homophobic gay-panic tropes, albeit it is a kid’s movie; still it feels (sadly) relevant to the modern struggle for gay rights and broader LGBTQ+ acceptance. Totally worth the watch.

reviews.filmTitle: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
paragraphs: It was poetic to kill Indy by rocket strike on that remote island
Maybe the first time Tom Hardy got super jacked for a role. He was so large in this movie, in basically every definition 😉
This movie really tries to make a nature vs. nurture argument at one point.
Funnier than the average comedy, and a fair sweet and wholesome tone.
“The floor is the new couch”- couldn’t agree more.
Wes Anderson’s least symmetrical movie, by a mile. This was a fun bop, with some great characters. Owen Wilson played the dimwitted asshole Dignan perfectly.

More flash than bang. Wes really wants you to remember that you’re watching a play, and pushes the format into frame a bit too much. It felt very much like The Drowsy Chaperone, interjecting anecdotes about characters amidst their paused scenes.
As always, it was cute and charming and lovely and full of wacky, zany characters. But I find myself wanting more out of Wes Anderson than his uber-pleasant symmetry and fantastic set designs.
This was a fine period horror, but a pretty non-Black Mirror way to end the season. My expectations we’re definitely too high, but I wanted to be wowed.
Ep 1: I like what this series has established so far. It’s an interesting, more adult plot, and I think Marvel has been at its best when doing spy thrillers.
I’m going to call Nick Fury being a Skrull now, and I think the swap happened immediately after the blip.
Ep 2: No one rocks a knit cap quite like Sam Jackson. Also, Nick Fury has a wife?!?!
Ep 3: First off, how dare you, Nick Fury, refer to a (decent looking) Full English Breakfast as “dog food”! Those are fighting words, I don’t care about the bants.
Ep 4: This whole “who’s a secret Skrull” thing is getting pretty annoying. I hope this doesn’t carry to future films and this series puts a wrap on that whole dynamic.
Ep 5: They had me so excited with the whole spy thriller angle, but now that it’s clear what everyone’s plans have been, I’m just disappointed by how surface-level and simple this all was.
This series has gotten more meh with each passing episode.
Ep 6: Headshots with no blood, that’s Disney for ya.
The fuck was that?
A decent overview of the early decades of Marvel Studios, as told by Stan Lee himself. It was nice to see how the characters matched up with the current events of the time.
Though the whole piece was told from Stan’s vantage, I felt they did an ok job of covering the ownership controversies with Steve Ditko and Jack Kirby.
What an excellently directed movie, a bold and beautiful debut for Celine Song. All three lead actors were likewise great, as was the story, though the direction definitely made the film.
My main complaint is that the movie had 5-10% too much sad, self-conscious Jewish energy.
Space, bitch
It was good but it didn’t give me the Black Mirror tickle that I’m looking for.
Black Mirror’s back, they got me with this one.
Every scene had a monologue, some worked, but all of them together were repetitive and got tiresome quickly.
Wasn’t “good enough to make me forget about Ezra Miller’s crimes”, in fact I think I just watched 140mins of Ezra committing petty crimes.
This one got a bit too high on its own supply
A really interesting subject with a super compelling, nearly continuous, first-person narrative. Being born in the 90s, I never really grasped how big of a star Arnold was in the 80s.
I really appreciated how open he was with the controversies of his life (except for the whole groping thing).

As someone who doesn’t care for football, Tom Brady, or really Boston sports in general, this was a very meh plane movie. The fact that Tom Brady produced this movie makes it so much stranger and more self-aggrandizing.

reviews.filmTitle: Hallelujah: Leonard Cohen, a Journey, a Song
paragraphs: This movie presumes that you are absolutely enamored with the masterpiece that is Hallelujah. If you’re not, wow is this movie a slog. They take the grueling time to investigate every step behind everyone who covered the song.

Two hours is way too long for a documentary for a single song. I think I like the song less after watching the film, and I sped through it at 1.25x speed. It may’ve been preferable to have just performed the 150 verse version of the song instead of making this movie.
Way too much clapplause and not enough laughs

I wouldn’t have watched this movie if not for Andrea Riseborough’s Oscar nomination drama, so congratulations, I guess it worked? All that being said, she did give a pretty good performance in a fairly straightforward, Oscar-baity movie. Ultimately this was a fine, but forgettable movie.
This documentary goes so much further than the TLC show, and ends with Madison Cawthorn and various plots to get homeschooled Christians into Congress and the Supreme Court.
Can’t believe Andrew slept through January 6th
Happy Pride 🌈

Watched this directly after watching the documentary on Harvey’s life, The Times of Harvey Milk, and this was a pretty faithful retelling. Sean Penn did a decent job playing the titular role, but it was odd that they kept in the “big ears” line.
Happy Pride 🌈

Harvey Milk was such an inspiring figure, murdered far too young for fighting for gay rights and recognition for all minority groups. Despite the tragically sad story, it was nice to see some history for SF, my home since 2018.

If you replace the word “gay” with “trans” nearly every talking point from the 70s is still being used today, and in that way this documentary felt extremely prescient. The work is certainly never done.

reviews.filmTitle: Black Mirror: Rachel, Jack and Ashley Too
paragraphs: I’ve long wanted a dark Hannah Montana 10 Year Later where she’s all washed up, and struggling to get by, and I think this Black Mirror take on a Disney Channel movie is about as close as we’ll ever get. And honestly, that depresses me.

I liked this movie, especially how often the movie put you into the deaf perspective. I thought it really worked and effectively conveyed the deaf family members’ experiences.

But I had one huge gripe with this movie: Ruby shouldn’t have been accepted to Berklee off that audition. She had so much preferential treatment in her audition. Do you think Miles would have choked if he had his music teacher accompanying him? That was so unfair.

If anything Berklee wanted to be generous to her after she forgot her music, they could’ve let her audition on another date when she was prepared. As someone who’s sat on the other side of auditions, this was bullshit. Now, apart from that, I thought that the rest of the film was excellent.
It’s no History of the World, but it’s still pretty damn great.
